intermediate.int_asana__task_open_length.statement: Counting crossed calendar-day boundaries is equivalent to counting full elapsed days for task open-length and assignment-duration metrics.
intermediate.int_asana__task_open_length.evidence_of_dependence: DATE_DIFF('day', t.created_at, CASE WHEN t.is_completed THEN t.completed_at ELSE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP END)
intermediate.int_asana__task_open_length.alternative: The contract says "integer number of full days (partial days are not counted)", whereas DATE_DIFF counts day boundaries even when less than a full day has elapsed.
intermediate.int_asana__task_open_length.reason: This affects all three duration metrics and downstream averages, validity checks, and performance results.

intermediate.int_asana__task_performance.statement: The latest story timestamp, or task creation timestamp when no story exists, is sufficient to determine last_activity_at without considering modified_at.
intermediate.int_asana__task_performance.evidence_of_dependence: COALESCE((SELECT MAX(s.created_at) ...), t.created_at) AS latest_story_at; latest_story_at AS last_activity_at
intermediate.int_asana__task_performance.alternative: The contract requires "the later of modified_at and the latest story timestamp for the task".
intermediate.int_asana__task_performance.reason: Ignoring recent task modifications can change activity scores, health scores, and the reported activity timestamp.

intermediate.int_asana__task_performance.statement: An overdue open task should receive urgency_score 5 regardless of how many days overdue it is.
intermediate.int_asana__task_performance.alternative: The contract specifies "due in 0–1 days → 5" and "else 1", which supports treating negative days-until-due as outside the listed ranges.
intermediate.int_asana__task_performance.reason: All overdue open tasks enter the highest urgency bucket under the implementation.

intermediate.int_asana__task_performance.statement: Completion timeliness can be determined from calendar dates alone without comparing completion and due times within the same day.
intermediate.int_asana__task_performance.evidence_of_dependence: WHEN is_completed AND completed_at::DATE <= due_date::DATE THEN 'completed_on_time'
intermediate.int_asana__task_performance.alternative: The contract specifies "completed_at on or before due_date" and "completed_at after due_date", reserving explicit calendar-date comparison for open-task overdue checks.
intermediate.int_asana__task_performance.reason: Tasks completed after their due time on the same day receive a different lifecycle category.

intermediate.int_asana__task_performance.statement: A missing response_time_days value contributes zero responsiveness points to health_score.
intermediate.int_asana__task_performance.reason: The contract permits missing response times but does not explicitly define their health-score contribution.

intermediate.int_asana__task_performance.statement: The performance-metrics output does not need an explicit ordering.
intermediate.int_asana__task_performance.alternative: The contract requires "Sort by health_score (descending), then urgency_score (descending), then task_id."
intermediate.int_asana__task_performance.reason: The query omits the required ordering even if its row values otherwise satisfy the contract.

intermediate.int_asana__task_assignee.statement: Passing staging task timestamps through unchanged satisfies the timezone-aware timestamp types required by the task-assignee model.
intermediate.int_asana__task_assignee.evidence_of_dependence: SELECT t.*, (t.assignee_user_id IS NOT NULL) AS has_assignee
intermediate.int_asana__task_assignee.alternative: Staging task timestamps are declared "TIMESTAMP", while task-assignee timestamp columns are declared "TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE".
intermediate.int_asana__task_assignee.reason: The selected columns retain staging types rather than establishing the intermediate model's declared types.

intermediate.int_asana__subtask_parent.statement: Passing parent task timestamps through unchanged satisfies the timezone-aware timestamp types required by the subtask-parent model.
intermediate.int_asana__subtask_parent.evidence_of_dependence: parent.due_date AS parent_due_date, parent.created_at AS parent_created_at
intermediate.int_asana__subtask_parent.alternative: The contract declares parent_due_date and parent_created_at as "TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE", while their staging sources are declared "TIMESTAMP".
intermediate.int_asana__subtask_parent.reason: The output inherits timezone-naive staging types without addressing the model's timezone-preservation requirement.

intermediate.int_asana__project_health_i.statement: Every project entering the health-indicator calculation has at least one completed task.
intermediate.int_asana__project_health_i.evidence_of_dependence: quality_tasks/NULLIF(completed_tasks,0) ... quality_percentage BETWEEN 0 AND 100 ... FROM final WHERE is_valid_record
intermediate.int_asana__project_health_i.alternative: The contract says percentages must be set to 0 "when denominator is 0"; the final SELECT applies COALESCE only after the validity filter has excluded rows with null percentages.
intermediate.int_asana__project_health_i.reason: Projects with no completed tasks, including projects with no tasks, would be excluded instead of receiving the specified zero percentages.

intermediate.int_asana__project_health_i.statement: Task creation and completion timestamps used for project recency counts are never in the future.
intermediate.int_asana__project_health_i.alternative: The contract requires tasks created or completed "within the last 7 days", whereas these conditions have no upper bound.
intermediate.int_asana__project_health_i.reason: Future timestamps would inflate recent activity counts and activity_percentage.

intermediate.int_asana__project_health_i.statement: Every retained project's creation calendar date is on or before the current date.
intermediate.int_asana__project_health_i.alternative: The contract describes project_age_days as a "non-negative integer", but the calculation and validity checks do not enforce that bound.
intermediate.int_asana__project_health_i.reason: Future-dated projects would produce negative ages contrary to the declared output constraint.

intermediate.int_asana__project_health_i.statement: Project deadline status should compare only the calendar date of project_due_date with today.
intermediate.int_asana__project_health_i.evidence_of_dependence: WHEN project_due_date::DATE>CURRENT_DATE THEN 'on_time' WHEN project_due_date::DATE=CURRENT_DATE THEN 'due_today'
intermediate.int_asana__project_health_i.alternative: The contract defines due_date as TIMESTAMP and says "on_time if due_date > today; due_today if equal", which could instead require direct timestamp comparison.
intermediate.int_asana__project_health_i.reason: Projects due later today can receive different deadline and forecast labels under the two interpretations.

intermediate.int_asana__user_productivit.statement: No tasks included in the productivity calculation have future creation timestamps.
intermediate.int_asana__user_productivit.alternative: The contract limits aggregation to tasks "created in the last 24 months" and output to "the last 12 months"; neither filter supplies an upper bound.
intermediate.int_asana__user_productivit.reason: Future-dated tasks could introduce future reporting months and alter cumulative metrics.

intermediate.int_asana__user_productivit.statement: The 24-month productivity computation window starts exactly 24 months before the current date rather than at a calendar-month boundary.
intermediate.int_asana__user_productivit.alternative: The contract describes "Monthly user productivity trends" using a "24-month history", which also permits a calendar-month-aligned interpretation.
intermediate.int_asana__user_productivit.reason: A partially included earliest month can change cumulative totals and historical window calculations.

intermediate.int_asana__user_productivit.statement: A timezone-naive month bucket satisfies the productivity model's timezone-aware activity_month requirement.
intermediate.int_asana__user_productivit.alternative: Staging declares created_at as "TIMESTAMP", while activity_month is declared "TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE" with the description "timezone preserved".
intermediate.int_asana__user_productivit.reason: The expression inherits a timezone-naive staging type rather than establishing the required output type.

intermediate.int_asana__user_productivit.statement: The last 12 months of productivity output means the current calendar month plus the preceding 11 calendar months.
intermediate.int_asana__user_productivit.alternative: The contract says "activity_month within the last 12 months", which could instead mean a cutoff at CURRENT_DATE minus 12 months.
intermediate.int_asana__user_productivit.reason: The interpretation determines whether an additional boundary month appears in the output.

marts.asana__user_performance_dashboard.statement: The ranked relation in the user performance dashboard exposes an is_valid_record column.
marts.asana__user_performance_dashboard.evidence_of_dependence: SELECT *,is_valid_record FROM ranked WHERE user_id IS NOT NULL
marts.asana__user_performance_dashboard.alternative: The execution log reports: "Binder Error: Referenced column \"is_valid_record\" not found in FROM clause!"
marts.asana__user_performance_dashboard.reason: The dashboard cannot be created unless the selected validity column is available.

marts.asana__user_performance_dashboard.statement: No dashboard user has at least three productivity-trend rows in the specified six-month historical baseline window.
marts.asana__user_performance_dashboard.alternative: The contract requires grouping historical productivity rows by user, requiring "count(*) >= 3", and computing arithmetic means; only missing baselines default to zero.
marts.asana__user_performance_dashboard.reason: Hardcoded baselines bypass required historical processing and can change baseline deltas and efficiency recommendations for every eligible user.

marts.asana__task.statement: Every staged task_id is safely castable to BIGINT.
marts.asana__task.evidence_of_dependence: LEFT JOIN intermediate.int_asana__task_followers fo ON t.task_id::BIGINT=fo.task_id
marts.asana__task.alternative: The contract says to compare numeric related identifiers using "the base task_id as text to align types", rather than converting the base identifier to a number.
marts.asana__task.reason: One nonnumeric or out-of-range task identifier can abort the task mart query.

marts.asana__task.statement: Every staged task_id has the canonical decimal representation of its numeric value.
marts.asana__task.alternative: The contract requires text-aligned comparisons, which would not equate an identifier such as "001" with numeric identifier 1 rendered as text.
marts.asana__task.reason: Numeric comparison can introduce related-model matches that the specified text comparison would reject.

marts.asana__task.statement: Passing staging task timestamps through unchanged satisfies the task mart's timezone-aware timestamp requirements.
marts.asana__task.alternative: The staging contract declares these timestamps as "TIMESTAMP", while the task mart declares them as "TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE".
marts.asana__task.reason: Direct selection retains timezone-naive staging types rather than establishing the mart's declared types.

marts.asana__daily_metrics.statement: UTC is the intended timezone for labeling daily buckets derived from the calendar dates of staging task timestamps.
marts.asana__daily_metrics.evidence_of_dependence: CAST(CAST(created_at AS DATE) AS TIMESTAMP) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS date_day
marts.asana__daily_metrics.alternative: The contract describes date_day as "midnight in its time zone" without specifying UTC; the previously observed staging parser converts offset-aware timestamps to naive timestamps in a session displaying "Asia/Singapore", so those calendar dates could instead require that timezone.
marts.asana__daily_metrics.reason: Explicit UTC labeling changes the timestamp instants representing daily buckets without establishing the intended reporting timezone.

marts.asana__daily_metrics.statement: The DuckDB session timezone is the intended timezone for interpreting daily task-count buckets.
marts.asana__daily_metrics.alternative: The contract describes date_day as "midnight in its time zone"; converting a timezone-naive date to TIMESTAMPTZ instead uses the session timezone.
marts.asana__daily_metrics.reason: An unintended session timezone changes the timestamp instants representing the reported days.

marts.asana__team_efficiency_metrics.statement: The staged project table contains a team_name column.
marts.asana__team_efficiency_metrics.evidence_of_dependence: SELECT p.team_id,p.team_name ... FROM staging.stg_asana__project p ... GROUP BY p.team_id,p.team_name
marts.asana__team_efficiency_metrics.alternative: The stg_asana__project contract lists team_id but no team_name; team_name is supplied by staging.stg_asana__team.
marts.asana__team_efficiency_metrics.reason: The project aggregation cannot execute if the referenced column is absent.

marts.asana__team_efficiency_metrics.statement: Joining assigned task rows to the user directory would produce no matched users for any team.
marts.asana__team_efficiency_metrics.alternative: The contract requires users linked by assignee_user_id=user_id, defaults their grade to 'developing_performer' and portfolio_task_count to 0, and counts distributions across joined task rows.
marts.asana__team_efficiency_metrics.reason: Omitting the user join replaces required task-weighted member distributions and averages with constants.

marts.asana__team_efficiency_metrics.statement: Both collaboration_efficiency_score and resource_optimization_score are zero for every team.
marts.asana__team_efficiency_metrics.alternative: The contract requires these scores to be calculated from performer, workload, and risk shares when unique_team_members is positive.
marts.asana__team_efficiency_metrics.reason: Hardcoding both components can materially change overall efficiency scores and downstream classifications.

marts.asana__team_efficiency_metrics.statement: Every team passing the implemented identifier and count checks also has avg_completion_rate and avg_quality_rate within the required non-null range of 0 through 100.
marts.asana__team_efficiency_metrics.evidence_of_dependence: (t.team_id IS NOT NULL AND t.team_name IS NOT NULL AND COALESCE(ps.total_projects,0)>=0 ... ) is_valid_record
marts.asana__team_efficiency_metrics.alternative: The contract requires avg_completion_rate and avg_quality_rate to be within [0,100] and says averages are NULL when no health values exist.
marts.asana__team_efficiency_metrics.reason: Teams without qualifying project health data can be retained despite failing the specified validation.

marts.asana__team_efficiency_metrics.statement: Project-size distribution in team efficiency metrics should be inferred from task-count bands rather than defaulted to medium_project.
marts.asana__team_efficiency_metrics.evidence_of_dependence: COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE h.total_tasks>100) enterprise_projects ... COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE h.total_tasks BETWEEN 21 AND 50) medium_projects
marts.asana__team_efficiency_metrics.alternative: The contract specifies 'project_health_summary: project health fields with project_size_category defaulted to medium_project'.
marts.asana__team_efficiency_metrics.reason: The inferred bands redistribute projects across size categories instead of applying the documented default.

marts.asana__project_analytics.statement: Time-management scoring may be based on completion and deadline status instead of schedule_forecast.
marts.asana__project_analytics.evidence_of_dependence: CASE WHEN completion_percentage=100 THEN 25 WHEN remaining_days<0 THEN 5 ELSE 12 END time_management_score
marts.asana__project_analytics.alternative: The contract maps schedule_forecast to scores: 'on_schedule 25; slight_delay 20; moderate_delay 15; significant_delay 10; overdue 5; else 12'.
marts.asana__project_analytics.reason: This substitution changes the time score, comprehensive score, and performance ranks.

marts.asana__project_analytics.statement: No project entering project analytics has a negative elapsed_days value.
marts.asana__project_analytics.alternative: The contract requires completion_rate_per_day to be NULL 'if elapsed_days is not positive', whereas NULLIF only handles zero.
marts.asana__project_analytics.reason: Future-created projects would receive negative completion rates instead of NULL.

marts.asana__project_analytics.statement: Every non-null project team_id has a matching staged team.
marts.asana__project_analytics.alternative: The analytics column description says team_id is 'null if no matching team'; selecting p.team_id preserves unmatched identifiers.
marts.asana__project_analytics.reason: Unmatched teams would leave non-null team identifiers where the output contract calls for NULL.

marts.asana__task_lifecycle_analysis.statement: Any task with a non-null completed_at timestamp is completed, even when is_completed is false.
marts.asana__task_lifecycle_analysis.alternative: The contract specifies using completed_at 'if completed, else to the current time'.
marts.asana__task_lifecycle_analysis.reason: An inconsistent open task would have its lifecycle duration and activity-rate denominator stopped at completed_at.

marts.asana__task_lifecycle_analysis.statement: An assigned open task with a missing modified_at timestamp should be classified as stagnant after failing the newly_assigned condition.
marts.asana__task_lifecycle_analysis.evidence_of_dependence: WHEN NOT is_completed AND assignee_user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'stagnant'
marts.asana__task_lifecycle_analysis.alternative: The contract requires 'last modification >7 days' for stagnant and provides an 'unknown_state' fallback.
marts.asana__task_lifecycle_analysis.reason: Missing modification timestamps are treated as evidence of staleness rather than an unknown state.

marts.asana__task_lifecycle_analysis.statement: A task missing performance metrics should receive an activity contribution equivalent to activity_score 1 in lifecycle_health_score.
marts.asana__task_lifecycle_analysis.alternative: The contract specifies 'Activity: activity_score*4' without defining a fallback score for missing metrics.
marts.asana__task_lifecycle_analysis.reason: The fallback changes health scores and permits scoring tasks whose performance metrics were excluded upstream.

marts.asana__task_lifecycle_analysis.statement: An open task without a due_date should receive five timeliness points in lifecycle_health_score.
marts.asana__task_lifecycle_analysis.evidence_of_dependence: WHEN due_date::DATE>CURRENT_DATE THEN 35 WHEN due_date::DATE=CURRENT_DATE THEN 25 ELSE 5 END
marts.asana__task_lifecycle_analysis.alternative: The contract assigns five points for 'overdue' but does not explicitly assign a timeliness contribution to tasks without a due date.
marts.asana__task_lifecycle_analysis.reason: The unspecified missing-deadline treatment affects lifecycle scores and score-based patterns.

marts.asana__task_lifecycle_analysis.statement: Passing staging task timestamps through unchanged satisfies the lifecycle mart's timezone-aware timestamp requirements.
marts.asana__task_lifecycle_analysis.alternative: Staging declares these fields as TIMESTAMP, while the lifecycle contract declares created_at, completed_at, and due_date as TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE.
marts.asana__task_lifecycle_analysis.reason: The mart inherits timezone-naive types without establishing the contracted timezone-aware types.

coverage_proxy.definition: Unique method2 contract-section table names; literal output key present, including an empty list. Schema prefix removed, lowercase, exact match. Not actual write detection.

stg_asana__user.problem: User names are trimmed even though the user staging contract does not prescribe name normalization, potentially changing downstream text that must retain original spacing.
stg_asana__user.reason: This can change displayed names and ordered name aggregations without an explicit correction rule.

stg_asana__user.problem: Duplicate user IDs are resolved arbitrarily rather than checking whether conflicting records are confirmed duplicates.
stg_asana__user.evidence_in_work: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY id) AS _rn
stg_asana__user.source: delete_row examples: ["Explicitly marked for deletion", "Confirmed duplicates", "Invalid primary keys"
stg_asana__user.reason: Conflicting names or emails could be selected nondeterministically and propagated to many models.

stg_asana__team.problem: Conflicting records with the same team ID are reduced to an arbitrary row without checking whether their attributes agree.
stg_asana__team.evidence_in_work: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY id) AS _rn
stg_asana__team.reason: Uniqueness is achieved, but the retained team name or organization could vary if duplicate IDs conflict.

stg_asana__project.problem: All project dates are parsed using only one exact timestamp format, so otherwise valid dates in another format may be nullified or cause entire projects to be dropped.
stg_asana__project.source: correct: "Automatically fix deterministic format issues such as ... standardized date formats"
stg_asana__project.reason: The agent sampled creation timestamps but did not establish that optional dates and all records share that format.

stg_asana__project.problem: Parsing zoned timestamps and immediately casting them to TIMESTAMP makes the stored wall-clock values depend on the DuckDB session time zone.
stg_asana__project.source: correct examples: ["LOWER(TRIM(email))", "standardize timezone formats", "normalize phone numbers"]
stg_asana__project.reason: Dates near midnight and subsequent deadline calculations may change across environments.

stg_asana__project.problem: Conflicting duplicate project IDs are resolved with no meaningful tie-breaker.
stg_asana__project.evidence_in_work: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY id) AS _rn
stg_asana__project.reason: An arbitrary owner, deadline, or status could drive downstream project analytics.

stg_asana__task.problem: Tasks with null names are not removed despite task_name being required.
stg_asana__task.evidence_in_work: WHERE id IS NOT NULL AND completed IS NOT NULL ...
stg_asana__task.reason: Invalid task rows can enter staging and several downstream models that do not revalidate names.

stg_asana__task.problem: The single timestamp parser may discard valid date-only due_on and start_on values or other valid timestamp formats.
stg_asana__task.evidence_in_work: COALESCE(CAST(TRY_STRPTIME(due_at, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f %z') AS TIMESTAMP), CAST(TRY_STRPTIME(due_on, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f %z') AS TIMESTAMP))
stg_asana__task.reason: Missing due dates would change lateness, urgency, lifecycle scores, and project risk.

stg_asana__task.problem: Task timestamps lose their time-zone information before reaching downstream models that declare zoned timestamps.
stg_asana__task.source: asana__task created_at: data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
stg_asana__task.reason: This creates a pipeline-wide type mismatch and session-dependent time interpretation.

stg_asana__task.problem: Floating-point identifier fields are cast directly to BIGINT without verifying that they are integral and accurately represented.
stg_asana__task.source: asana_start.yaml: assignee_id: DOUBLE; completed_by_id: DOUBLE; parent_id: DOUBLE
stg_asana__task.reason: Fractional or precision-damaged IDs could silently become incorrect user or parent references.

stg_asana__task.problem: Duplicate task IDs are resolved arbitrarily without comparing task versions or attributes.
stg_asana__task.evidence_in_work: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY id) AS _rn
stg_asana__task.reason: Conflicting duplicates could produce nondeterministic completion, assignment, and timing metrics.

stg_asana__story.problem: The staging type whitelist removes system and comment values that downstream action classification requires, an unresolved contract incompatibility that should be checked.
stg_asana__story.source: int_asana__task_story: "If story_type equals 'system'"; "Else if story_type equals 'comment'"
stg_asana__story.reason: The observed action output is exclusively other, eliminating comment and assignment metrics throughout the pipeline despite literal compliance with the staging whitelist.

stg_asana__story.problem: Story timestamps are accepted only in one exact format rather than using robust parsing across valid source formats.
stg_asana__story.reason: Valid differently formatted events would be deleted and could change activity history.

stg_asana__story.problem: Conflicting duplicate story IDs are arbitrarily collapsed.
stg_asana__story.evidence_in_work: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY id) AS _rn
stg_asana__story.reason: Different event text, authors, or timestamps could be retained across executions.

stg_asana__tag.problem: The exact-format timestamp parser can remove tags with valid creation timestamps in other formats.
stg_asana__tag.evidence_in_work: CAST(TRY_STRPTIME(created_at, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f %z') AS TIMESTAMP) IS NOT NULL
stg_asana__tag.reason: Dropped tags affect both tag attributes and task tag-name lookups.

stg_asana__tag.problem: Conflicting duplicate tag IDs are reduced to an arbitrary record.
stg_asana__tag.evidence_in_work: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY id) AS _rn
stg_asana__tag.reason: The retained tag name or attributes could be unstable if duplicate keys conflict.

stg_asana__section.problem: The filter checks raw project_id rather than the parsed BIGINT, allowing unparseable non-null project references to become null in a required column.
stg_asana__section.evidence_in_work: TRY_CAST(project_id AS BIGINT) project_id ... AND project_id IS NOT NULL

int_jira__sprint_performance_analytics.statement: Velocity trends may be left NULL instead of calculating their moving average.

int_jira__project_health_scoring.statement: Every project receives 25 in each health dimension under the documented scoring rules.

int_jira__project_health_scoring.statement: No project has issue creations or resolutions in any of the specified recent reporting windows.

int_jira__issue_lifecycle_analysis.statement: The documented standard deviation for activity_variance is the sample standard deviation.

int_jira__user_activity_metrics.statement: Rows sharing the same user_id and activity_date retain a consistent relative order between the windows in w and the subsequent lag windows in v.

int_jira__user_activity_metrics.statement: User activity consistency scores may retain DuckDB's inferred rounded numeric type instead of DOUBLE.

int_jira__user_activity_metrics.statement: Explicit user_id and activity_date ordering is unnecessary for the user activity result.

jira__sprint_enhanced.statement: For every sprint ID, sprint name, start, end, completion, and board metadata are constant across daily rows.

jira__daily_sprint_issue_history.statement: Explicit ordering by sprint_id, issue_id, and date_day is unnecessary for the daily sprint history output.

jira__issue_enhanced.statement: Issue keys are unique across the enhanced issue source rows.

jira__team_performance_dashboard.statement: No collaboration or sprint aggregate can match a dashboard user's all_projects project identifier.

jira__team_performance_dashboard.reason: Hard-coded nulls rely on an unverified exclusion of matching project IDs and bypass all associated source processing.

jira__team_performance_dashboard.statement: A missing average close-time-days metric should become zero in both dashboard activity scores.

jira__team_performance_dashboard.reason: This changes unavailable activity information into a populated numeric score.

jira__project_risk_assessment.statement: Every project has no delayed unresolved issues and qualifies for zero scope risk.

jira__project_risk_assessment.statement: Every project has zero net recent issue growth, zero resolution-velocity change, and 100 percent team stability.

jira__project_risk_assessment.statement: Every project has zero distinct issue types, zero components, zero external links, and zero sprint adoption.

jira__project_risk_assessment.statement: Every project qualifies for Standard Priority under the strategic-priority rules.

jira__project_risk_assessment.reason: Even the query's fixed risk total yields a probability that can trigger nondefault recommendations for sufficiently valuable projects.

staging timestamp outputs.statement: Casting the offset-normalized strings directly to TIMESTAMP preserves the timezone meaning required for cross-table comparisons and calendar dates.

staging.stg_jira__user.problem: Duplicate user IDs are not removed or otherwise reconciled despite the required uniqueness constraint.
staging.stg_jira__user.evidence_in_work: from raw.user where id is not null
staging.stg_jira__user.reason: Duplicates would multiply comments, issues, and downstream user metrics, although the sampled output had unique IDs.

staging.stg_jira__user.problem: Missing or blank display names are replaced with IDs and existing names are trimmed rather than simply validating the required display name.
staging.stg_jira__user.reason: This invents display names and changes text used in profiles and conversations without an explicit correction rule.

staging.stg_jira__project.problem: Duplicate project IDs are resolved by an arbitrary tied ordering that may retain an incorrect project record.
staging.stg_jira__project.evidence_in_work: row_number() over(partition by id order by id)=1
staging.stg_jira__project.reason: Conflicting duplicate attributes could change project names and lead assignments, but duplicates were not demonstrated.

staging.stg_jira__issue.problem: Estimate and time-spent fields prefer underscore-prefixed columns without establishing whether those columns are the intended seconds measures.
staging.stg_jira__issue.source: raw.issue columns include _original_estimate, original_estimate, _remaining_estimate, remaining_estimate, _time_spent, time_spent
staging.stg_jira__issue.reason: Choosing the wrong parallel measure would affect estimates, hours, and financial metrics throughout the pipeline.

staging.stg_jira__issue.problem: Timezone suffixes are stripped rather than interpreted when converting issue timestamps.
staging.stg_jira__issue.reason: The observed +0800 values become naive local times, potentially shifting runtime ages and comparisons across offsets.

staging.stg_jira__issue.problem: Required issue keys and successfully parsed required timestamps are not validated.
staging.stg_jira__issue.evidence_in_work: where id is not null and created is not null and updated is not null and project is not null
staging.stg_jira__issue.reason: A non-null malformed timestamp can become NULL through try_cast, while a NULL key passes the filter.

staging.stg_jira__issue.problem: Negative estimates, time spent, and work ratios are carried into downstream models whose contracts require non-negative values.
staging.stg_jira__issue.source: original_estimate_seconds IS NULL OR original_estimate_seconds >= 0; work_ratio IS NULL OR work_ratio >= 0
staging.stg_jira__issue.reason: Invalid measures would violate analytical model tests and distort duration and investment summaries.

staging.stg_jira__issue.problem: Duplicate issues are selected using lexicographic raw timestamp ordering rather than parsed chronological ordering.
staging.stg_jira__issue.evidence_in_work: partition by id order by updated desc nulls last
staging.stg_jira__issue.reason: Mixed timestamp formats or offsets could select an older duplicate, although sampled issue IDs were unique.

staging.stg_jira__sprint.problem: Sprint timestamps lose their timezone offsets during parsing.
staging.stg_jira__sprint.source: Cleaned sprint data with validated date ranges and consistent naming
staging.stg_jira__sprint.reason: Sprint boundaries and runtime active flags can be shifted when offsets are meaningful.

staging.stg_jira__sprint.problem: Sprint ID uniqueness is not enforced.
staging.stg_jira__sprint.evidence_in_work: from raw.sprint where id is not null and trim(id)<>''
staging.stg_jira__sprint.reason: Duplicate sprints would change synthetic assignments and could duplicate sprint-level outputs.

staging.stg_jira__sprint.problem: Reversed sprint date ranges are not checked before downstream non-negative duration calculations.
staging.stg_jira__sprint.reason: Invalid ranges could produce negative planned durations and incorrect snapshot selection.

staging.stg_jira__comment.problem: Comment timezone offsets are discarded rather than normalized.
staging.stg_jira__comment.reason: Activity dates and seven-day interaction intervals may be wrong across differing offsets.

staging.stg_jira__comment.problem: The required created_at field may become NULL after parsing even though the raw created string is non-null.
staging.stg_jira__comment.reason: Malformed dates can survive staging and disappear from conversations or create invalid activity dates.

staging.stg_jira__comment.problem: Duplicate comment IDs are resolved by earliest raw creation text with no check for conflicting bodies or updates.
staging.stg_jira__comment.evidence_in_work: row_number() over(partition by id order by created)=1
staging.stg_jira__comment.reason: The retained comment may not represent the latest valid content.

staging.stg_jira__issue_field_history.reason: Event ordering, assignment durations, and daily snapshots can be incorrect when offsets differ.

staging.stg_jira__issue_field_history.problem: NULL is_active values are retained despite the non-null constraint.
staging.stg_jira__issue_field_history.reason: Unvalidated activity flags can silently exclude history from active-field analyses.

staging.stg_jira__issue_field_history.problem: Filtering non-null raw time strings does not guarantee a non-null parsed updated_at.
staging.stg_jira__issue_field_history.reason: Malformed times can survive into latest-event selection and date-based metrics.

staging.stg_jira__field.problem: NULL field names are not rejected despite the required non-null field_name.

staging.stg_jira__field.reason: Name-based Epic, sprint, and story-point identification would fail for these fields.

staging.stg_jira__field.problem: Conflicting duplicate field definitions are selected arbitrarily.
staging.stg_jira__field.evidence_in_work: partition by id order by id
staging.stg_jira__field.reason: The chosen name can change all history interpretation for that field.

staging.stg_jira__issue_link.reason: Direction-sensitive consumers could reverse relationships, although most shown metrics inspect both endpoints.

staging.stg_jira__status.problem: Rows with NULL status names are retained.
staging.stg_jira__status.evidence_in_work: name status_name ... where id is not null
staging.stg_jira__status.reason: Required status labels can remain missing throughout issue reporting.

staging.stg_jira__status.problem: Duplicate status IDs with conflicting attributes are resolved by arbitrary tied ordering.
staging.stg_jira__status.evidence_in_work: partition by id order by id
staging.stg_jira__status.reason: The selected category and label may not be the correct definition.

staging.stg_jira__priority.evidence_in_work: name priority_name ... where id is not null

marts.jira__team_performance_dashboard.reason: Required sprint processing is omitted and would fail to populate any legitimate matching project group.

marts.jira__team_performance_dashboard.problem: Missing average close-time metrics are converted to zero without a specified fallback.
marts.jira__team_performance_dashboard.source: Set avg_daily_activity_score and avg_weekly_activity_score from average close time days
marts.jira__team_performance_dashboard.reason: Missing duration information is presented as a genuine zero activity score.

marts.jira__team_performance_dashboard.problem: performance_tier is hard-coded rather than classified from the computed score.
marts.jira__team_performance_dashboard.source: Top Performer (score ≥85), Strong Performer (≥70), Average Performer (≥50), else Needs Improvement
marts.jira__team_performance_dashboard.reason: The implementation cannot reflect improved scores if data produces them.

marts.jira__team_performance_dashboard.problem: poor_estimation is fixed false rather than evaluated from estimate accuracy.
marts.jira__team_performance_dashboard.source: poor_estimation is true when estimate accuracy ratio > 2
marts.jira__team_performance_dashboard.reason: Eligible poor-estimation signals can never be surfaced.

marts.jira__team_performance_dashboard.problem: The required score, project-name, and user-name ordering is omitted.
marts.jira__team_performance_dashboard.source: ordered by overall_performance_score descending, then project_name, then user_display_name
marts.jira__team_performance_dashboard.reason: Direct SQL presentation differs from the dashboard contract.

marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.problem: The required project self-join and its duplicate output rows are omitted.
marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.source: One or more identical rows per issue_id (project-level self-join propagates duplicates)
marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.reason: The output grain and row multiplicity differ substantially from the explicitly required result.

marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.problem: Comparative lifecycle and comment metrics are not computed, leaving deviation and outlier fields NULL.
marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.source: project average/median/p75 lifecycle days ... project average comments
marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.reason: Anomaly detection and its downstream decisions lack their required inputs.

marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.problem: Deviation risk and collaboration and efficiency opportunities are fixed at zero.
marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.reason: Total risk and opportunity scores omit meaningful components.

marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.problem: intelligence_score is fixed at 50 instead of using risks, opportunities, and completion probability.
marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.reason: The main ranking metric cannot distinguish issues.

marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.problem: health_status is always Healthy despite nonzero calculated risk scores.
marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.source: ≥25 Critical; ≥15 High Risk; ≥8 Medium Risk; >0 Low Risk; else Healthy
marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.reason: At-risk issues are explicitly mislabeled as healthy.

marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.source: age_risk_score>0 and assignment_risk_score>0 → 'Urgent: Assign and Expedite'
marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.reason: Urgent assignment and collaboration interventions are suppressed.
The output cannot prioritize time-sensitive issues.

marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.problem: strategic_importance is always Standard rather than recognizing critical priorities and Epics.
marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.reason: Strategically important work is not identified.

marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.problem: Completion timeframe tests assignee_name rather than assignee_user_id for the Normal lifecycle branch.
marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.evidence_in_work: when assignee_name is null then 'Requires Assignment' else 'Within 2 Weeks'
marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.reason: Assigned issues whose user lookup fails can be incorrectly treated as requiring assignment.

marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.problem: The required intelligence-score and risk-score ordering is absent.
marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.source: ordered by intelligence_score DESC, total_risk_score DESC
marts.jira__issue_intelligence_analytics.reason: Direct SQL output does not provide the specified prioritized ranking.

marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.problem: Schedule risk is fixed at zero even though delayed issues are calculated.
marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.reason: Projects with old unresolved issues can receive materially understated total risk.

marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.problem: Resource risk and team stability are constants rather than using recent active-assignee counts.
marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.reason: All projects are assigned maximum resource risk regardless of team size.

marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.problem: Recent and prior issue trend calculations are omitted and net growth and velocity change are fixed to zero.
marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.reason: Growth and delivery changes cannot influence risk or reporting.

marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.problem: Scope risk is hard-coded zero rather than calculated from net growth and total issues.
marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.reason: Even zero net growth normally maps to a nonzero scope bucket for nonempty projects.

marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.problem: Issue links, components, and sprint history are unused and complexity outputs are fixed to zero.
marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.reason: Complexity risk and adoption metrics ignore all required relationship data.

marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.problem: unique_issue_types is fixed zero despite issue type data already being read.
marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.reason: A directly computable project complexity measure is absent.

marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.problem: Primary risk driver and intervention are constants instead of classifications from the computed risk dimensions.
marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.evidence_in_work: 'Resource Constraints' primary_risk_driver,'Regular Monitoring and Minor Adjustments' recommended_intervention
marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.source: primary_risk_driver = label of the maximum among the five risk scores
marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.reason: Recommendations cannot respond to schedule, scope, or complexity problems.

marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.source: success_probability ≥ 0.8 and estimated_project_value_points > 50 → 'High Priority - High Success'
marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.reason: High-value projects can miss an explicitly required prioritization rule.

marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.problem: Timeline and budget predictions implement only a subset of the required ordered rules.
marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.evidence_in_work: 'Moderate Delay Risk' timeline_prediction ... else 'Within Budget Expectations'
marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.source: schedule_risk_score ≥ 15 → 'Moderate Budget Impact'; total_risk_score > 70 → 'Significant Delay Risk'
marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.reason: Predictions would remain incorrect once actual risk scores vary.

marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.problem: The required descending total-risk and ascending success-probability ordering is omitted.
marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.source: ordered by total_risk_score descending, then success_probability ascending
marts.jira__project_risk_assessment.reason: The direct SQL result does not prioritize project risk as requested.

marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.problem: The commenter interaction network and its three-interaction filter are not constructed.
marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.source: Pair comments by different authors ... within 7 days ... Keep only pairs with at least 3 interaction instances
marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.reason: The core engagement network is replaced by an assumption that every stakeholder has no connections.

marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.problem: Outbound and inbound influence metrics are always NULL.
marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.source: Compute interaction strength ... total inbound interaction strength
marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.reason: Influential collaborators cannot be identified or scored.

marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.problem: Every stakeholder is labeled a Slow responder without calculating assigned resolution days.
marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.reason: Response quality and delivery-risk classifications lose their required basis.

marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.problem: Engagement depth and total engagement are always NULL instead of being calculated when network data exists.
marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.source: Total engagement score = breadth + depth + quality + impact
marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.reason: The main engagement measure is unavailable for every active user.

marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.problem: Quality and impact scores are fixed zero even where issue workload alone should award impact points.
marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.reason: Known assignment counts are not used in mandatory scoring.

marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.problem: Breadth scoring omits the direct-network-connection contribution.
marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.source: 3 points per project involved + 5 points per cross-functional project + up to 10 points for direct connections
marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.reason: Stakeholders with few projects but strong networks can be materially underscored.

marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.problem: Stakeholder archetype and influence level are constants rather than ordered classifications.
marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.source: Heavy Executor (issues assigned >20); Requirements Driver (issues reported >20)
marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.reason: Even classifications supported by the already calculated issue counts are not applied.

marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.problem: Engagement risk is always Healthy Engagement, suppressing delivery and isolation conditions.
marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.source: Delivery Risk (Slow responder and issues assigned >10); Isolation Risk (connections <2 and projects involved >1)
marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.reason: Stakeholders meeting the model's own risk inputs are still labeled healthy.

marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.problem: Strategic value, engagement strategy, and development opportunity are hard-coded instead of using the required ordered mappings.
marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.source: Network Building (connections <3); ... recommended strategy ... Performance Support
marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.reason: The final actionable recommendations do not reflect calculated stakeholder characteristics.

marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.problem: The required strategic-value and total-engagement ordering is absent.
marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.source: ordered by strategic value score descending, then total engagement score descending
marts.jira__stakeholder_engagement_insig.reason: Direct SQL presentation is not the requested prioritization.

staging.stg_marketo__campaigns.evidence_of_dependence: ('program_id','program_id','VARCHAR') is projected with CAST, without format validation or nullification.
staging.stg_marketo__campaigns.alternative: The campaign contract requires "program_id IS NULL OR program_id ~ '^MAR[0-9]+$'" and specifies "on_failure: nullify_field".
staging.stg_marketo__campaigns.reason: Unvalidated identifiers could violate the staging contract and alter downstream program attribution.

staging.stg_marketo__campaigns.statement: The active field in raw.marketo_campaign contains no null values.
staging.stg_marketo__campaigns.evidence_of_dependence: ('is_active','active','BOOLEAN') is handled by CAST(active AS BOOLEAN), with no COALESCE.
staging.stg_marketo__campaigns.alternative: The campaign contract requires "is_active = COALESCE(is_active, FALSE)" and describes the correction as "Default NULL active flag to FALSE".
staging.stg_marketo__campaigns.reason: Any null source flag would remain null instead of becoming the required non-null false value.

staging.stg_marketo__program.statement: The staging models may expose their created_timestamp, updated_timestamp, and campaign recurrence timestamps as VARCHAR rather than TIMESTAMP.
staging.stg_marketo__program.evidence_of_dependence: All four model definitions include ('created_timestamp','created_at','VARCHAR') and ('updated_timestamp','updated_at','VARCHAR'); campaigns also includes ('recurrence_start_at','recurrence_start_at','VARCHAR').
staging.stg_marketo__program.alternative: The staging governance specifies "timestamp_format: TIMESTAMP", supporting typed timestamps rather than strings.
staging.stg_marketo__program.reason: This affects timestamp columns across four staging models and can change downstream date comparisons and calculations.

staging.stg_marketo__program.statement: Every non-null program start_date and end_date has its intended calendar date represented by its first ten characters in a format DuckDB can cast to DATE.
staging.stg_marketo__program.evidence_of_dependence: TRY_CAST(SUBSTR(start_date, 1, 10) AS DATE) and TRY_CAST(SUBSTR(end_date, 1, 10) AS DATE)
staging.stg_marketo__program.reason: Other date representations would silently become null or yield a different date after truncation.

staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.statement: The is_most_recent_version column does not need to be supplied by the email-template-history staging model.
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.evidence_of_dependence: The email-template projection includes version, operational, subject, and from_email, but does not project is_most_recent_version.
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.alternative: The email-template-history contract explicitly lists "name: is_most_recent_version" with "data_type: BOOLEAN".
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.reason: Omitting a contracted column can prevent downstream consumers from selecting the current template version.

staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.statement: The greatest version value within each template ID identifies its most recent version.
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.evidence_of_dependence: (version = MAX(version) OVER (PARTITION BY id)) AS is_most_recent_version
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.reason: The contract requires the flag but does not establish how recency is determined, which can affect current-template selection.

staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.statement: The staging models may expose their created_timestamp, updated_timestamp, and campaign recurrence timestamps as VARCHAR rather than TIMESTAMP.
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.evidence_of_dependence: All four model definitions include ('created_timestamp','created_at','VARCHAR') and ('updated_timestamp','updated_at','VARCHAR'); campaigns also includes ('recurrence_start_at','recurrence_start_at','VARCHAR').
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.alternative: The staging governance specifies "timestamp_format: TIMESTAMP", supporting typed timestamps rather than strings.
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.reason: This affects timestamp columns across four staging models and can change downstream date comparisons and calculations.

staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.statement: Each raw email-template-history row already has a non-null version.
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.evidence_of_dependence: ('version','version','DOUBLE') is projected, while where remains empty for this model.
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.alternative: The email-template-history contract specifies "constraints: [not_null]" for version.
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.reason: A null source version would pass through despite being essential to the contracted template-version grain.

staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.statement: Ordering the raw version values produces the same maximum as ordering their contracted DOUBLE representations.
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.reason: If raw versions are strings, their maximum can differ from the numeric maximum used to identify the latest version.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_send_email.statement: An email send's email_send_id is the raw send activity's id, without any additional derivation.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_send_email.evidence_of_dependence: The send-email projection maps both ('activity_id','id','VARCHAR') and ('email_send_id','id','VARCHAR').
staging.stg_marketo__activity_send_email.reason: If email_send_id denotes a different business key, downstream send attribution or joins could use the wrong grain.

marts.marketo__email_sends.statement: Each email_template_id referenced by a send matches at most one row in staging.stg_marketo__email_template_history.
marts.marketo__email_sends.alternative: The staging contract defines the history grain as "One row per email template version", allowing multiple rows per template, while the email-sends contract specifies "One row per email_send_id".
marts.marketo__email_sends.reason: Multiple matching versions multiply send rows and consequently inflate engagement metrics throughout downstream marts.

intermediate.marketo__change_data_detail.statement: Every lead-and-day group in the change events contains at least one matching metadata row with a non-null rest_name_xf.
intermediate.marketo__change_data_detail.evidence_of_dependence: LOWER(d.rest_name_xf) AS field_name ... BOOL_OR(field_name='email') AS email_c
intermediate.marketo__change_data_detail.alternative: The contract explicitly allows unmatched metadata and says "NULL primary_attribute_column never matches; groups may have all flags FALSE", whereas an all-null BOOL_OR input produces NULL.
intermediate.marketo__change_data_detail.reason: Entirely unmatched groups would produce null flags instead of the required false flags.

intermediate.marketo__change_data_scd.statement: A missing or null field-change flag should be treated as false when determining SCD backfill boundaries.
intermediate.marketo__change_data_scd.alternative: The SCD contract says a group continues only when "the field value is null and the corresponding details flag is false"; it does not explicitly equate a missing or null flag with false.
intermediate.marketo__change_data_scd.reason: This interpretation can carry values across boundaries that a strict false-only interpretation would retain.

intermediate.marketo__change_data_pivot.statement: For each lead and day, no two distinct primary_attribute_value_id values map to the same tracked REST attribute token with conflicting selected old_value values.
intermediate.marketo__change_data_pivot.reason: If multiple attribute IDs map to the same token, MAX selects by string value rather than by the earliest change for that target attribute.

intermediate.marketo__lead_calendar_spin.statement: Each non-null created_timestamp used by the lead calendar spine begins with a valid YYYY-MM-DD representation of its intended creation date.
intermediate.marketo__lead_calendar_spin.alternative: The contract requires using "the date portion of created_timestamp" without specifying that the date always occupies its first ten characters.
intermediate.marketo__lead_calendar_spin.reason: Other valid timestamp representations could silently exclude leads or assign an incorrect start date.

marts.marketo__email_templates.statement: Selecting the highest version and then the greatest updated_timestamp for each email_template_id is an acceptable replacement for filtering metadata by is_most_recent_version.
marts.marketo__email_templates.evidence_of_dependence: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY email_template_id ORDER BY version DESC, updated_timestamp DESC) AS version_rank ... WHERE t.version_rank = 1
marts.marketo__email_templates.alternative: The contract says to "keep only rows marked as the most recent version"; the new code ignores that flag and emits "TRUE AS is_most_recent_version".
marts.marketo__email_templates.reason: The replacement can select different template metadata or include templates with no marked current version.

marts.marketo__email_templates.statement: Exactly one history row per email_template_id is marked is_most_recent_version.
marts.marketo__email_templates.reason: Missing or multiple current-version flags would omit templates or violate the required one-row-per-template grain.

marts.marketo__email_templates.statement: Rows tied for the highest version and updated_timestamp within an email_template_id have identical output metadata.
marts.marketo__email_templates.evidence_of_dependence: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY email_template_id ORDER BY version DESC, updated_timestamp DESC)
marts.marketo__email_templates.reason: Conflicting tied rows would make the selected template metadata arbitrary.

marts.marketo__leads.statement: The staged lead base contains at most one row per lead_id.
marts.marketo__leads.evidence_of_dependence: SELECT l.* ... FROM staging.stg_marketo__lead l LEFT JOIN deleted d USING(lead_id)
marts.marketo__leads.alternative: The intermediate lead contract explicitly notes that "duplicates on lead_id are preserved", so downstream uniqueness cannot be inferred from that intermediate model.
marts.marketo__leads.reason: The mart preserves base duplicates despite requiring exactly one row per lead.

marts.marketo__lead_history.statement: The calendar-spine-to-SCD join produces at most one row per lead_id and date_day.
marts.marketo__lead_history.evidence_of_dependence: FROM spine s LEFT JOIN changes c ON s.lead_id=c.lead_id AND s.date_day=c.valid_to
marts.marketo__lead_history.alternative: The SCD contract states "no enforced uniqueness" and "multiple rows may exist for a lead and date", while the lead calendar spine preserves source duplicates.
marts.marketo__lead_history.reason: Duplicate matches violate the daily history grain and make the descending-date partition boundaries ambiguous.

marts.marketo__lead_intelligence_simple.statement: Leads with no email engagement may be assigned the rfm_segment 'Inactive' rather than 'Unknown'.
marts.marketo__lead_intelligence_simple.evidence_of_dependence: Segmentation runs over metrics after the left join and zero defaults, with "ELSE 'Inactive' END AS rfm_segment".
marts.marketo__lead_intelligence_simple.alternative: The contract says to derive segmentation from aggregated engagement and specifies "rfm_segment defaults to \"Unknown\" ... when segmentation is missing".
marts.marketo__lead_intelligence_simple.reason: Every eligible lead without engagement receives a different segment under this interpretation.

marts.marketo__lead_intelligence_simple.statement: All creation and last-engagement dates used by eligible leads are on or before the execution date.
marts.marketo__lead_intelligence_simple.evidence_of_dependence: DATE_DIFF('day',CAST(last_email_sent_at AS DATE),CURRENT_DATE) and DATE_DIFF('day',TRY_CAST(SUBSTR(created_timestamp,1,10) AS DATE),CURRENT_DATE) are returned without a lower bound.
marts.marketo__lead_intelligence_simple.reason: Future source dates would produce negative values despite the contracted nonnegative tests.

marts.marketo__lead_intelligence_simple.statement: A missing or unparseable lead creation date may be represented by a lead_tenure_days value of zero.
marts.marketo__lead_intelligence_simple.alternative: The contract defines tenure as "the calendar days between the lead's created date and today" and supplies no zero fallback for missing or invalid creation dates.
marts.marketo__lead_intelligence_simple.reason: The fallback makes unknown tenure indistinguishable from a lead created today.

marts.marketo__operational_health_simple.statement: Per-campaign open rate should be calculated from the delivery flag rather than the open flag.
marts.marketo__operational_health_simple.evidence_of_dependence: AVG(CASE WHEN was_delivered THEN 100.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS open_rate
marts.marketo__operational_health_simple.alternative: The contract specifies "open rate = average of opened (as percent)", supporting use of was_opened.
marts.marketo__operational_health_simple.reason: This changes campaign health counts, the composite score, and potentially the recommendation.

marts.marketo__operational_health_simple.statement: The chosen point allocations and thresholds implement the required composite health score.
marts.marketo__operational_health_simple.evidence_of_dependence: Deliverability, engagement, and campaign mix each receive 25, 20, 15, or 5 points, while stability receives 25, 15, or 5 points.
marts.marketo__operational_health_simple.alternative: The contract describes an "integer 35–100" score but does not establish these particular thresholds or allocations; the implemented allocations permit a total of 20.
marts.marketo__operational_health_simple.reason: Unestablished scoring rules can materially change the snapshot's principal summary metric.

marts.marketo__operational_health_simple.statement: Every matched email-send row has a non-null activity_id.
marts.marketo__operational_health_simple.evidence_of_dependence: COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE activity_id IS NULL) AS inactive_leads; CASE WHEN activity_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE ... END
marts.marketo__operational_health_simple.alternative: The contract defines inactive leads as "rows with no matching send", while the email-sends contract explicitly guarantees non-null email_send_id rather than activity_id.
marts.marketo__operational_health_simple.reason: A matched send with a null activity identifier would be classified as inactivity and lose its engagement score.

marts.marketo__operational_health_simple.statement: No email sends have future timestamps that would enter the recent-period metrics.
marts.marketo__operational_health_simple.target: marts.marketo__operational_health_simple recent-delivery and seven-day trend metrics
marts.marketo__operational_health_simple.alternative: The contract describes activity "over the last 30 days" and "within the last 7 days", which supports excluding activity after the snapshot time.
marts.marketo__operational_health_simple.reason: Without upper bounds, future records can change recent delivery rates and trend averages.

marts.marketo__operational_health_simple.statement: The last-seven-days trend window consists of today and the preceding six calendar dates.
marts.marketo__operational_health_simple.alternative: The contract says "within the last 7 days" without specifying whether this means today plus six dates or the preceding seven completed dates.
marts.marketo__operational_health_simple.reason: Different window boundaries can change all three recent trend averages.

result.md.statement: Non-send email activities may use their own raw activity IDs as email_send_id for the send-level engagement joins.
result.md.target: result.md: described email activity key mapping
result.md.evidence_of_dependence: “其他活动表也按原始活动 ID 输出 email_send_id”
result.md.alternative: The email-sends contract requires joining aggregated opens, bounces, clicks, deliveries, and unsubscribes “by email_send_id”, which supports a shared send identifier rather than independently assigned event identifiers.
result.md.reason: If independent event IDs do not identify the corresponding send, engagement attribution throughout the marts changes.

result.md.statement: Keeping the newest updated record for duplicate entity IDs and the earliest record for duplicate activity IDs is the required way to resolve conflicting staging duplicates.
result.md.evidence_of_dependence: “对重复主键保留更新时间较新的记录（活动重复时保留较早记录）”
result.md.alternative: The staging quality actions authorize removal of “Confirmed duplicates”, but the supplied specifications do not establish these survivor-selection rules for conflicting records.
result.md.reason: The selected survivor determines which attributes and activity values reach downstream models.

result.md.statement: The raw merge_ids field has the same meaning and representation as the contracted merged_lead_ids field.
result.md.reason: A different interpretation of the merge payload would change merged-into values and merge flags.

result.md.statement: The absence of null email_send_id values after staging and deduplication establishes that raw send IDs contain no nulls.
result.md.target: result.md: source send ID nullability claim
result.md.evidence_of_dependence: “email_send_id 空值 0、重复 0（源数据的 send ID 均非空）” follows a check against intermediate.marketo__email_sends_deduped.
result.md.alternative: The same report says staging removes “缺少关键 ID/时间/必需属性的行”, so raw null IDs could have been removed before this check.
result.md.reason: The downstream check does not establish whether source records were discarded for missing IDs.

result.md.statement: The two engagement flags omitted from the null check, was_bounced and was_unsubscribed, also contain no null values.
result.md.evidence_of_dependence: The report states “engagement flags ... 空值均为 0”, while the query checks only “was_opened is null or was_clicked is null or was_delivered is null”.
result.md.reason: The stated validation covers more flags than the displayed check establishes.

coverage_proxy.definition: Unique method2 contract-section table names; literal output key present, including an empty list. Schema prefix removed, lowercase, exact match. Not actual write detection.

utils.marketo__calendar_spine.problem: The calendar's end date is assumed to be today even though no visible utility specification establishes that bound.
utils.marketo__calendar_spine.source: The upper bound of dates is defined only by the calendar spine; no additional end-date filter is applied.
utils.marketo__calendar_spine.reason: An incorrect utility range changes the coverage of every downstream lead calendar.

staging.stg_marketo__lead.problem: Non-normalized emails are corrected and retained rather than deleted as the field-specific failure action requires.
staging.stg_marketo__lead.reason: This changes which leads enter every downstream lead model.

staging.stg_marketo__lead.problem: Duplicate lead IDs are resolved using textual updated_at ordering, which may not select the chronologically latest record when formats or offsets differ.
staging.stg_marketo__lead.evidence_in_work: PARTITION BY id ORDER BY updated_at DESC NULLS LAST
staging.stg_marketo__lead.reason: Incorrect survivor selection would propagate stale profile attributes.

staging.stg_marketo__campaigns.problem: Casting fractional configuration values directly to BIGINT may silently round quantities rather than validate their intended meaning.
staging.stg_marketo__campaigns.reason: The observed source contains fractional values for fields whose output represents integer configuration.

staging.stg_marketo__campaigns.problem: Boolean source interval fields are converted to 0 or 1 without checking whether the source encoding actually represents numeric intervals.
staging.stg_marketo__campaigns.evidence_in_work: CAST(qualification_rule_interval AS BIGINT); CAST(recurrence_interval AS BIGINT)
staging.stg_marketo__campaigns.source: qualification_rule_interval ... Numeric interval used in qualification rules.
staging.stg_marketo__campaigns.reason: The source schema exposes booleans, so the intended interval information may not be recoverable by a cast.

staging.stg_marketo__campaigns.problem: Duplicate campaigns are resolved by string timestamp ordering rather than parsed chronological ordering.
staging.stg_marketo__campaigns.evidence_in_work: PARTITION BY id ORDER BY updated_at DESC NULLS LAST
staging.stg_marketo__campaigns.source: grain: "One row per unique campaign in Marketo"
staging.stg_marketo__campaigns.reason: This matters only if duplicate records have differing timestamp formats or offsets.

staging.stg_marketo__program.problem: Required program IDs, channels, and timestamps are not checked for nulls.
staging.stg_marketo__program.reason: Invalid required attributes would pass through directly into the program dimension.

staging.stg_marketo__program.problem: The unique program grain is not enforced or checked.
staging.stg_marketo__program.reason: Duplicate source IDs would create duplicate program dimension rows.

staging.stg_marketo__program.problem: Taking only the first ten characters of dates assumes an ISO year-month-day prefix and silently nullifies other formats.
staging.stg_marketo__program.reason: This is plausible for the observed source conventions but was not checked for program dates.

staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.problem: The required non-null template ID, name, version, and timestamps are not validated.
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.source: email_template_id, email_template_name, version, created_timestamp, updated_timestamp: constraints: [not_null]
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.reason: Invalid metadata would survive staging and affect both template selection and send enrichment.

staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.problem: The maximum-version expression can mark multiple rows as most recent for the same template.
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.evidence_in_work: (version = MAX(version) OVER (PARTITION BY id)) AS is_most_recent_version
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.source: One row per email_template_id (most recent version only)
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.reason: Tied maximum versions make the staging flag inconsistent with the downstream single-row expectation.

staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.problem: The from_email regex appears over-escaped in the Python-generated SQL and may nullify valid sender addresses.
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.evidence_in_work: s.replace('CAST(from_email AS VARCHAR) AS from_email', 'CASE WHEN from_email IS NULL OR from_email ~ ...')
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.reason: An extra backslash in the emitted DuckDB regex could remove sender addresses across the entire table.

staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.problem: Template-version uniqueness is not enforced or tested.
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.source: grain: "One row per email template version"
staging.stg_marketo__email_template_hist.reason: Duplicate versions can multiply send fact rows when history is joined by template ID.

staging.stg_marketo__lead_describe.problem: rest_name_xf is assumed to be an unchanged copy of restname without verifying compatibility with the tracked-field tokens.
staging.stg_marketo__lead_describe.reason: Unexpected underscores, spaces, or alternate REST names would suppress historical changes for affected fields.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_send_email.problem: email_send_id is assumed to equal the send activity's own ID without an established cross-activity send-key definition.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_send_email.reason: This key controls send deduplication and all subsequent engagement associations.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_send_email.problem: The not-null activity_type_id constraint is not enforced.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_send_email.evidence_in_work: WHERE id IS NOT NULL AND lead_id IS NOT NULL AND activity_date IS NOT NULL
staging.stg_marketo__activity_send_email.reason: Rows with missing required activity types remain in the send fact.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_send_email.problem: Non-null but unparseable activity dates can become null timestamps without being removed.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_send_email.reason: The current send timestamp check passes, but the SQL does not enforce the constraint for other input formats.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_send_email.problem: Timestamp-with-zone parsing followed by a TIMESTAMP cast makes the resulting wall-clock time depend on the session time zone.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_send_email.reason: Different execution environments could change daily and weekly assignments.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_open_email.problem: The open event's own activity ID is used as email_send_id rather than a verified reference to the originating send.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_open_email.source: Email open activities aggregated by email_send_id
staging.stg_marketo__activity_open_email.reason: Event-local IDs can prevent all opens from matching sends.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_open_email.problem: The activity timestamp parser accepts only one format and retains rows whose parsing fails.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_open_email.reason: Other valid date formats would silently lose timestamps.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_click_emai.problem: The click event's own activity ID is used as email_send_id without verifying a relationship to the original send.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_click_emai.source: Counts click activity rows per email_send_id
staging.stg_marketo__activity_click_emai.reason: Unrelated event IDs can eliminate click attribution to sends.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_click_emai.problem: Unparseable non-null activity dates remain as null timestamps.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_click_emai.reason: The parser assumes one exact source format without checking failures.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_email_deli.problem: Delivery activity IDs are treated as send IDs without confirming that they identify the originating send.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_email_deli.source: Counts delivery activity rows per email_send_id
staging.stg_marketo__activity_email_deli.reason: This can make every send appear undelivered despite the delivery source containing 14,000 rows.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_email_deli.problem: Date parsing failures are retained as null timestamps.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_email_deli.reason: A non-null raw date does not establish successful timestamp conversion.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_email_boun.problem: Bounce activity IDs are assigned to email_send_id without verifying a send reference.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_email_boun.source: Counts bounced email activities per email_send_id
staging.stg_marketo__activity_email_boun.reason: Bounce counts may never attach to the send fact.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_email_boun.problem: The timestamp conversion can silently yield null while the source row is retained.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_unsubscrib.problem: Unsubscribe event IDs are used as email_send_id without establishing a relationship to send IDs.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_unsubscrib.source: Count of unsubscribe activity rows per email_send_id
staging.stg_marketo__activity_unsubscrib.reason: Unsubscribe activity can disappear from all send-based analytics.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_unsubscrib.problem: Only raw date presence is checked, allowing failed timestamp conversions to remain.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_unsubscrib.reason: Malformed or differently formatted dates silently become null.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_change_dat.problem: Rows with null activity_type_id are not removed despite its required status.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_change_dat.evidence_in_work: WHERE id IS NOT NULL AND lead_id IS NOT NULL AND activity_date IS NOT NULL
staging.stg_marketo__activity_change_dat.reason: The staging table does not guarantee its declared required fields.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_change_dat.problem: Failed timestamp parsing is not filtered, potentially causing historical events to disappear in later date filters.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_change_dat.reason: A null parsed timestamp prevents an event from entering daily historical models.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_change_dat.problem: Converting a zoned timestamp to an unzoned timestamp without setting the session time zone may change the calendar day across environments.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_change_dat.source: Derive date_day as the calendar date of activity_timestamp.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_change_dat.reason: Changes near midnight could move between daily history records.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_merge_lead.problem: The required activity_type_id constraint is not enforced.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_merge_lead.evidence_in_work: WHERE id IS NOT NULL AND lead_id IS NOT NULL AND activity_date IS NOT NULL
staging.stg_marketo__activity_merge_lead.reason: Incomplete merge records can survive staging.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_merge_lead.problem: Timestamp parsing failures remain in the table despite the not-null timestamp requirement.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_merge_lead.reason: Raw non-null dates do not guarantee valid output timestamps.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_delete_lea.problem: The not-null activity_type_id requirement is omitted from row validation.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_delete_lea.evidence_in_work: WHERE id IS NOT NULL AND lead_id IS NOT NULL AND activity_date IS NOT NULL
staging.stg_marketo__activity_delete_lea.reason: The output can violate its required schema.

staging.stg_marketo__activity_delete_lea.problem: The date parser can produce null activity_timestamp values that are not removed.
staging.stg_marketo__activity_delete_lea.reason: The SQL checks raw date presence rather than conversion success.

intermediate.int_marketo__lead.problem: Its lead population can include emails that should have triggered staging deletion because the upstream lead model normalizes them instead.
intermediate.int_marketo__lead.reason: The local pass-through logic is correct, but the inherited population may differ from the contract.

intermediate.marketo__email_sends_dedupe.problem: Deduplication uses an assumed activity-local key that may not identify repeated records of the same email send.
intermediate.marketo__email_sends_dedupe.evidence_in_work: PARTITION BY email_send_id ORDER BY activity_timestamp ASC
intermediate.marketo__email_sends_dedupe.source: Deduplicates email send events ... per email_send_id
intermediate.marketo__email_sends_dedupe.reason: If activity IDs differ across representations of one send, the intended deduplication never occurs.

intermediate.marketo__opens__by_sent_ema.problem: The grouping key inherits each open event's own ID, potentially producing event-level rather than send-level aggregates.
intermediate.marketo__opens__by_sent_ema.source: One row per email_send_id present in staging.stg_marketo__activity_open_email

intermediate.marketo__clicks__by_sent_em.problem: Click aggregation inherits an event-local ID rather than a verified send identifier.

intermediate.marketo__change_data_detail.problem: Groups containing only unmatched or null metadata produce null flags instead of false.

intermediate.marketo__change_data_detail.problem: Tracked-field matching depends on the unverified restname-to-rest_name_xf pass-through.
intermediate.marketo__change_data_detail.reason: Names differing by more than case would cause genuine changes to go unflagged.

intermediate.marketo__change_data_pivot.problem: The pivot assumes copied REST names match the contract's attribute tokens after lowercasing alone.

intermediate.marketo__change_data_pivot.reason: An incorrect upstream transformed-name mapping would nullify historical attribute values.

intermediate.marketo__change_data_scd.problem: Missing details flags are converted to false, allowing backfill through boundaries where the specification's explicit false condition is not satisfied.

intermediate.marketo__lead_calendar_spin.problem: The created-date extraction assumes the first ten characters always contain an ISO date and silently excludes leads if that assumption fails.

marts.marketo__email_sends.reason: This can make all engagement counts zero even though the raw engagement tables contain substantial activity.

marts.marketo__email_sends.problem: The template-history join may multiply sends when a template has multiple versions, conflicting with the declared one-row-per-send grain.
