stg_salesforce__opportunity.statement: The opportunity's six derived timing columns can be read directly from raw.opportunity without computation.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.alternative: The inspected raw.opportunity schema lacks is_created_this_month, is_created_this_quarter, days_since_created, days_to_close, is_closed_this_month, and is_closed_this_quarter, although the contract requires them.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.reason: The generated model depends on unavailable source expressions for required output columns.

stg_salesforce__opportunity.statement: The opportunity's own raw id is the intended source for its account_id.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.alternative: The contract validates account_id against raw.account, and raw.opportunity has a distinct account_id column.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.reason: Every opportunity's account relationship depends on this interpretation.

stg_salesforce__opportunity.statement: Raw opportunity account_id values already satisfy the required ID-format and raw.account membership checks, so projecting them directly requires no nullification.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.alternative: The contract requires nullify_field when account_id fails either "account_id IS NULL OR account_id ~ '^[A-Za-z0-9]{15,18}$'" or "account_id IS NULL OR account_id IN (SELECT id FROM raw.account)".
stg_salesforce__opportunity.reason: Correcting the source column alone does not establish that invalid account references are handled as required.

stg_salesforce__opportunity.statement: All opportunity close_date values already satisfy the contract's historical, future, and creation-date bounds.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.alternative: The contract requires nullification outside 1900 through CURRENT_DATE plus one year or before created_date.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.reason: Unchecked dates affect both pipeline reporting and sales-cycle calculations.

stg_salesforce__opportunity.statement: All opportunity owner_id values already satisfy the required format and raw.user membership checks.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.evidence_of_dependence: The opportunity filter list checks id, deletion, and name but not owner_id.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.alternative: The contract requires invalid owner_id values to be nullified after format and raw.user membership validation.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.reason: Invalid owner references can alter attribution and enrichment.

stg_salesforce__opportunity.statement: The opportunity closure-period flags should depend only on close_date, without requiring is_closed to be true.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.evidence_of_dependence: (close_date is not null and year(close_date)=year(current_date) and month(close_date)=month(current_date)) as is_closed_this_month
stg_salesforce__opportunity.alternative: The names "is_closed_this_month" and "is_closed_this_quarter" support requiring an actually closed opportunity, rather than merely a scheduled close date in the period.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.reason: Open opportunities scheduled to close this period can be treated as closed-period opportunities by downstream metrics.

stg_salesforce__opportunity.statement: Opportunity timing fields may continue to use the raw close_date even when the projected close_date is nullified by validation.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.evidence_of_dependence: The edit replaces only "try_cast(close_date as DATE) as close_date," with a validation CASE expression.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.alternative: The contract describes "Cleaned sales opportunity records with validated amounts, dates, and stage information"; deriving timing fields from the validated close_date would avoid reporting durations or closure-period flags for rejected dates.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.reason: Invalid source dates can still influence downstream timing metrics despite being removed from the visible close_date field.

stg_salesforce__opportunity.statement: days_to_close should measure the creation-to-close-date interval for open opportunities as well as closed opportunities.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.evidence_of_dependence: case when close_date is not null and created_date is not null then date_diff('day', created_date::date, close_date::date) end as days_to_close
stg_salesforce__opportunity.reason: The contract lists the field without defining whether it represents a completed sales cycle, a scheduled cycle, or remaining time to close.

stg_salesforce__opportunity.statement: The creation-period flags should use calendar months and quarters evaluated on the pipeline execution date.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.reason: A fiscal-period or reporting-as-of interpretation would classify a different set of opportunities.

stg_salesforce__opportunity.statement: DuckDB BIGINT date differences are acceptable for the staging timing fields declared as INTEGER.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.evidence_of_dependence: date_diff('day', created_date::date, current_date) end as days_since_created
stg_salesforce__opportunity.alternative: The contract declares both "days_since_created" and "days_to_close" with "data_type: INTEGER".
stg_salesforce__opportunity.reason: The new expressions do not explicitly cast their results to the contracted output types.

stg_salesforce__user.statement: The user's own raw id is the intended source for its account_id, contact_id, and user_role_id.
stg_salesforce__user.alternative: raw.user contains separate account_id, contact_id, and user_role_id columns corresponding to the contract's columns.
stg_salesforce__user.reason: The global mapping replaces three different user relationships with the user's identity.

stg_salesforce__user.statement: Deduplicating users by user_id alone is sufficient to guarantee username uniqueness.
stg_salesforce__user.alternative: The contract declares both user_id and username "[not_null, unique]".
stg_salesforce__user.reason: Different user ids sharing a username are not addressed by the generated deduplication.

stg_salesforce__user.statement: Keeping an arbitrary raw row for each user id is an acceptable duplicate-resolution policy.
stg_salesforce__user.evidence_of_dependence: qualify row_number() over (partition by {key} order by {key}) = 1
stg_salesforce__user.reason: Conflicting duplicate users can produce nondeterministic attributes and relationships.

stg_salesforce__opportunity_line_item.statement: The line item's own raw id is the intended source for its opportunity_id and product_2_id.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_line_item.alternative: raw.opportunity_line_item exposes distinct opportunity_id and product_2_id columns, which the contract also names.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_line_item.reason: Both principal relationships of every line item depend on this mapping.

stg_salesforce__opportunity_line_item.statement: Deleted opportunity line items may remain in staging.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_line_item.alternative: The contract specifies "NOT COALESCE(is_deleted, false)" with on_failure: delete_row.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_line_item.reason: Retaining deleted line items can inflate downstream product and revenue analysis.

stg_salesforce__order.statement: The order's own raw id is the intended source for its account_id.
stg_salesforce__order.alternative: The inspected raw.order_data schema contains a distinct account_id column.
stg_salesforce__order.reason: This changes the account association of every generated order.

stg_salesforce__contact_history.statement: The contact history record's raw id is the intended source for its account_id.
stg_salesforce__contact_history.alternative: raw.contact_history has a separate account_id column in addition to id.
stg_salesforce__contact_history.reason: Historical contact-to-account relationships are replaced throughout the output.

stg_salesforce__contact_history.statement: Only one history version per contact needs to be retained to satisfy history_unique_key uniqueness.
stg_salesforce__contact_history.evidence_of_dependence: 'history_unique_key':'id'; qualify row_number() over (partition by {key} order by {key}) = 1
stg_salesforce__contact_history.alternative: The contract describes "contact history records tracking changes to contact data over time" and requires history_unique_key to be unique.
stg_salesforce__contact_history.reason: Entity-level deduplication can remove most contact history.

stg_salesforce__contact_history.statement: The combination of contact_id, _fivetran_start, and _fivetran_end distinguishes every retained contact history record that requires a distinct history_unique_key.
stg_salesforce__contact_history.evidence_of_dependence: md5(concat_ws('|', coalesce(cast(contact_id as varchar), ''), coalesce(cast(_fivetran_start as varchar), ''), coalesce(cast(_fivetran_end as varchar), ''))) as history_unique_key
stg_salesforce__contact_history.reason: Distinct retained versions sharing these inputs would receive the same key despite the contract's uniqueness constraint.

stg_salesforce__contact_history.statement: The contact history created_date represents the Fivetran version start timestamp.
stg_salesforce__contact_history.evidence_of_dependence: if name in ('created_date',) and n.endswith('_history'): expr='_fivetran_start'
stg_salesforce__contact_history.reason: Historical analyses depend on the intended meaning of this timestamp.

stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.statement: raw.opportunity_history contains an account_account_id column that supplies the required account_id.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.alternative: The available raw.opportunity_history schema lists account_id, not account_account_id.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.reason: The changed account relationship expression depends on an unavailable source column.

stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.statement: The opportunity history last_modified_date can be read directly from raw.opportunity_history.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.alternative: The inspected raw.opportunity_history schema lacks last_modified_date but includes _fivetran_synced and _fivetran_start.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.reason: The model requires a source expression not present in the inspected table.

stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.statement: The opportunity history record's raw id is the intended source for its account_id.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.alternative: raw.opportunity_history has a separate account_id column in addition to id.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.reason: Historical opportunity-to-account relationships depend on this mapping.

stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.statement: The opportunity history created_date should use _fivetran_start rather than the source created_date.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.evidence_of_dependence: if name in ('created_date',) and n.endswith('_history'): expr='_fivetran_start'
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.alternative: The inspected raw.opportunity_history schema includes a distinct created_date column.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.reason: Replacing business creation time with version start can change historical sales-cycle calculations.

stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.statement: Opportunity history rows with a NULL raw id should be excluded.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.evidence_of_dependence: from raw.opportunity_history where id is not null
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.alternative: The history contract lists opportunity_id without a not_null constraint or a delete_row validation rule.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.reason: The filter removes historical records under an exclusion policy not established by the history contract.

stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.statement: Setting last_modified_date to NULL for every opportunity history row is acceptable under the contract.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.evidence_of_dependence: replace('last_modified_date as last_modified_date','cast(null as timestamp) as last_modified_date')
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.reason: Absence of the identically named raw column does not establish the intended treatment of available history timestamps.

stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.statement: Entity id plus _fivetran_start and _fivetran_end is sufficient to identify each opportunity history row.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.evidence_of_dependence: md5(concat_ws('|', coalesce(cast({keyid} as varchar), ''), coalesce(cast(_fivetran_start as varchar), ''), coalesce(cast(_fivetran_end as varchar), '')))
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.reason: Different versions with identical identity inputs would receive the same generated key.

stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.statement: Opportunity history probabilities outside the range 0–100 should be nullified.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.evidence_of_dependence: case when try_cast(probability as DECIMAL) between 0 and 100 then try_cast(probability as DECIMAL) else null end as probability
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.alternative: The history contract specifies only data_type: DECIMAL for probability, whereas the current-opportunity contract explicitly supplies the range validation rules.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.reason: Extending current-record validation to history can erase historical values that the history contract does not instruct the pipeline to nullify.

stg_salesforce__account_history.statement: raw.account_history contains an account_id column that can supply the staging account_id.
stg_salesforce__account_history.alternative: The supplied raw.account_history schema contains "id", not "account_id"; execution reports: "Column 'account_id' referenced that exists in the SELECT clause - but this column cannot be referenced before it is defined".
stg_salesforce__account_history.reason: This source-column assumption prevents the account history staging table and its dependent daily-history mart from being created.

stg_salesforce__account_history.statement: raw.account_history contains an account_account_id column that supplies the required account_id.
stg_salesforce__account_history.alternative: The available raw.account_history schema contains id but neither account_account_id nor account_id; the contract identifies raw.account_history as the source for this model.
stg_salesforce__account_history.reason: The changed projection depends on a source column absent from the supplied schema.

stg_salesforce__account_history.statement: Only one history version per account needs to be retained to satisfy history_unique_key uniqueness.
stg_salesforce__account_history.evidence_of_dependence: 'history_unique_key':'id'; qualify row_number() over (partition by {key} order by {key}) = 1
stg_salesforce__account_history.alternative: The contract describes "account history records tracking changes to account data over time" and declares history_unique_key, rather than account_id, unique.
stg_salesforce__account_history.reason: Deduplicating by entity id can discard nearly all historical versions.

stg_salesforce__account_history.statement: The combination of id, _fivetran_start, and _fivetran_end distinguishes every retained account history record requiring a distinct history_unique_key.
stg_salesforce__account_history.evidence_of_dependence: md5(concat_ws('|', coalesce(cast(id as varchar), ''), coalesce(cast(_fivetran_start as varchar), ''), coalesce(cast(_fivetran_end as varchar), ''))) as history_unique_key; the edit removes the QUALIFY deduplication.
stg_salesforce__account_history.reason: Retained records sharing these inputs would receive identical keys despite the contract's uniqueness constraint.

stg_salesforce__account_history.statement: The account history created_date represents the Fivetran version start timestamp.
stg_salesforce__account_history.evidence_of_dependence: if name in ('created_date',) and n.endswith('_history'): expr='_fivetran_start'
stg_salesforce__account_history.reason: Version validity time and business creation time have different analytical meanings.

stg_salesforce__account_history.statement: Null entity ids should cause account history rows to be removed.
stg_salesforce__account_history.evidence_of_dependence: if n=='stg_salesforce__account_history': filters=['id is not null']
stg_salesforce__account_history.alternative: The account history contract requires history_unique_key to be non-null but does not declare account_id non-null.
stg_salesforce__account_history.reason: This adds a row-exclusion policy beyond the explicit history constraints.

stg_salesforce__event.statement: All retained events already satisfy end_date_time being no earlier than start_date_time.
stg_salesforce__event.evidence_of_dependence: if n=='stg_salesforce__event': filters=['id is not null','owner_id is not null']
stg_salesforce__event.alternative: The contract requires delete_row when "end_date_time IS NULL OR end_date_time >= start_date_time" fails.
stg_salesforce__event.reason: The required rejection of temporally invalid events is absent.

stg_salesforce__event.statement: Event start and end timestamps already satisfy their contract range limits.
stg_salesforce__event.alternative: The contract requires nullification outside 2000–2100 and additionally limits start_date_time to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP plus one year.
stg_salesforce__event.reason: Out-of-range calendar values would survive unchanged.

stg_salesforce__event.statement: Comparing raw event end_date_time and start_date_time directly produces the same chronological ordering as comparing their parsed TIMESTAMP values.
stg_salesforce__event.reason: The projections explicitly parse timestamps, but the rejection predicate relies on unverified raw types and representations.

stg_salesforce__event.statement: Event end-before-start validation should be applied to original timestamps before out-of-range timestamps are nullified.
stg_salesforce__event.evidence_of_dependence: and (end_date_time is null or start_date_time is null or end_date_time >= start_date_time)
stg_salesforce__event.alternative: The contract separately requires out-of-range start_date_time and end_date_time values to undergo "nullify_field"; applying those corrections first could prevent a row from failing the ordering check.
stg_salesforce__event.reason: The processing order determines whether events with invalid timestamps are removed entirely or retained with nullified fields.

stg_salesforce__event.statement: Keeping an arbitrary row per event id is an acceptable duplicate-resolution policy.
stg_salesforce__event.evidence_of_dependence: qualify row_number() over (partition by {key} order by {key}) = 1
stg_salesforce__event.reason: Conflicting event versions can produce different dates and ownership.

stg_salesforce__lead.statement: The status whitelist should be applied to raw lead status before any trimming.
stg_salesforce__lead.evidence_of_dependence: 'status in (\'Open - Not Contacted\', \'Working - Contacted\', \'Closed - Converted\', \'Closed - Not Converted\')'
stg_salesforce__lead.alternative: The contract specifies "status = TRIM(status)" with on_failure: correct, supporting correction of whitespace before validation.
stg_salesforce__lead.reason: Otherwise-correct leads with padded statuses would be removed rather than repaired.

stg_salesforce__lead.statement: Every retained lead already has a non-null owner_id.
stg_salesforce__lead.evidence_of_dependence: The lead filter list checks id, last_name, name, and status but not owner_id.
stg_salesforce__lead.reason: The model relies on source cleanliness to satisfy an explicit required field.

stg_salesforce__lead.statement: Keeping an arbitrary row per lead id is an acceptable duplicate-resolution policy.
stg_salesforce__lead.evidence_of_dependence: qualify row_number() over (partition by {key} order by {key}) = 1
stg_salesforce__lead.reason: Conflicting versions can change status and conversion attributes without a defined selection rule.

stg_salesforce__task.statement: The status whitelist should be applied to raw task status before any trimming.
stg_salesforce__task.evidence_of_dependence: 'status in (\'Not Started\', \'In Progress\', \'Completed\', \'Waiting on someone else\', \'Deferred\')'
stg_salesforce__task.alternative: The contract specifies "status = TRIM(status)" with on_failure: correct.
stg_salesforce__task.reason: Padded valid statuses would cause entire tasks to be discarded.

stg_salesforce__task.statement: Keeping an arbitrary row per task id is an acceptable duplicate-resolution policy.
stg_salesforce__task.evidence_of_dependence: qualify row_number() over (partition by {key} order by {key}) = 1
stg_salesforce__task.reason: Conflicting duplicate tasks can change completion and activity reporting.

stg_salesforce__user_role.statement: Keeping an arbitrary row per user role id is an acceptable duplicate-resolution policy.
stg_salesforce__user_role.evidence_of_dependence: qualify row_number() over (partition by {key} order by {key}) = 1
stg_salesforce__user_role.reason: Duplicate role versions could disagree on hierarchy or role name.

stg_salesforce__product_2.statement: Keeping an arbitrary row per product id is an acceptable duplicate-resolution policy.
stg_salesforce__product_2.evidence_of_dependence: qualify row_number() over (partition by {key} order by {key}) = 1
stg_salesforce__product_2.reason: Conflicting product versions can change catalog classifications and active status.

int_salesforce__account_enhanced.statement: Non-deleted staging accounts have at most one row per account_id.
int_salesforce__account_enhanced.reason: Without deduplication, repeated account IDs violate the required grain and can multiply downstream opportunity rows.

int_salesforce__account_enhanced.statement: Accounts with a NULL is_deleted flag should be included as non-deleted accounts and have their output flag set to FALSE.
int_salesforce__account_enhanced.evidence_of_dependence: where not coalesce(is_deleted, false) ... coalesce(is_deleted, false) as is_deleted
int_salesforce__account_enhanced.alternative: The intermediate contract says "keep only rows where is_deleted is false", while the staging contract permits NULL deletion flags through "NOT COALESCE(is_deleted, false)".
int_salesforce__account_enhanced.reason: This interpretation expands the account population beyond a strict FALSE filter.

int_salesforce__opportunity_pipeline.statement: Opportunities with a NULL is_deleted flag should be included as non-deleted opportunities and have their output flag set to FALSE.
int_salesforce__opportunity_pipeline.evidence_of_dependence: where not coalesce(is_deleted, false) ... coalesce(op.is_deleted, false) as is_deleted
int_salesforce__opportunity_pipeline.alternative: The intermediate contract specifies "filtered to is_deleted = false", while staging permits NULL flags through "NOT COALESCE(is_deleted, false)".
int_salesforce__opportunity_pipeline.reason: Including NULL-flag opportunities can change pipeline counts and monetary totals.

int_salesforce__activity_summary.statement: The staging account table contains at most one matching row per active account_id.
int_salesforce__activity_summary.evidence_of_dependence: select account_id from staging.stg_salesforce__account ... left join staging.stg_salesforce__account s on a.account_id = s.account_id
int_salesforce__activity_summary.reason: Duplicate IDs can multiply rows through both the account set and the second account join, violating the required grain.

int_salesforce__activity_summary.statement: Tasks with a NULL is_deleted flag should contribute to activity metrics.
int_salesforce__activity_summary.evidence_of_dependence: from staging.stg_salesforce__task where not coalesce(is_deleted, false)
int_salesforce__activity_summary.alternative: The contract says to keep task rows "where is_deleted=false".
int_salesforce__activity_summary.reason: These additional tasks can change activity counts, recency, owner counts, and engagement defaults.

int_salesforce__activity_summary.statement: Events with a NULL is_deleted flag should contribute to activity metrics.
int_salesforce__activity_summary.evidence_of_dependence: from staging.stg_salesforce__event where not coalesce(is_deleted, false)
int_salesforce__activity_summary.alternative: The contract says to keep event rows "where is_deleted=false".
int_salesforce__activity_summary.reason: These additional events can change activity counts, recency, owner counts, and engagement defaults.

int_salesforce__activity_summary.statement: Accounts with a NULL is_deleted flag belong in the activity summary's active account population.
int_salesforce__activity_summary.evidence_of_dependence: select account_id from staging.stg_salesforce__account where not coalesce(is_deleted, false)
int_salesforce__activity_summary.alternative: The contract defines the output population as accounts "where is_deleted=false".
int_salesforce__activity_summary.reason: This changes which accounts receive summary rows.

int_salesforce__lead_conversion_funnel.statement: Leads with a NULL is_deleted flag should be included in the lead conversion funnel.
int_salesforce__lead_conversion_funnel.evidence_of_dependence: select * from staging.stg_salesforce__lead where not coalesce(is_deleted, false)
int_salesforce__lead_conversion_funnel.alternative: The contract says "include only leads where is_deleted = false" and describes all output rows as having "is_deleted=false".
int_salesforce__lead_conversion_funnel.reason: This expands the funnel population and allows NULL deletion flags into its output.

int_salesforce__lead_conversion_funnel.statement: Passing through annual_revenue as DECIMAL(18,3) is acceptable for the funnel's required DECIMAL(18,2) output.
int_salesforce__lead_conversion_funnel.alternative: The staging contract declares annual_revenue as "DECIMAL(18,3)", while the funnel column declares "DECIMAL(18,2)".
int_salesforce__lead_conversion_funnel.reason: Without an explicit conversion, the output retains a different monetary scale from the declared schema.

int_salesforce__lead_conversion_funnel.statement: A converted identifier is considered present whenever it is non-NULL, even if it is an empty or whitespace-only string.
int_salesforce__lead_conversion_funnel.evidence_of_dependence: converted_account_id is not null and converted_contact_id is not null and converted_opportunity_id is not null
int_salesforce__lead_conversion_funnel.alternative: The contract requires all three converted IDs to be "present", which could instead require nonempty identifiers.
int_salesforce__lead_conversion_funnel.reason: The interpretation determines whether leads with blank conversion references are marked complete.

int_salesforce__user_performance.statement: Each retained staging opportunity row represents a distinct opportunity for user-level counting.
int_salesforce__user_performance.reason: Repeated opportunity records would inflate counts and sums and could change performance tiers.

int_salesforce__user_performance.statement: Leads with a NULL is_deleted flag should contribute to user performance metrics.
int_salesforce__user_performance.evidence_of_dependence: from staging.stg_salesforce__lead where not coalesce(is_deleted, false) and owner_id is not null group by owner_id
int_salesforce__user_performance.alternative: The contract describes total_leads as the "Count of non-deleted leads owned by the user", and the lead funnel explicitly uses "is_deleted = false" for non-deleted leads.
int_salesforce__user_performance.reason: Including unknown deletion states changes lead totals, converted totals, and conversion rates.

int_salesforce__user_performance.statement: BIGINT counts are acceptable for won_opportunities and converted_leads despite their declared HUGEINT output types.
int_salesforce__user_performance.evidence_of_dependence: count(*) filter (where is_won = true) as won_opportunities; count(*) filter (where is_converted = true) as converted_leads
int_salesforce__user_performance.alternative: The contract declares both won_opportunities and converted_leads as "HUGEINT".
int_salesforce__user_performance.reason: The count expressions and subsequent coalescing do not explicitly produce the contracted types.

int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.statement: Joining opportunities to accounts is unnecessary for the owner aggregation.
int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.evidence_of_dependence: from staging.stg_salesforce__opportunity o left join staging.stg_salesforce__user u on o.owner_id=u.user_id
int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.alternative: The business logic explicitly requires "Opportunity to Account on account_id"; account matches could also multiply opportunity rows because account_id uniqueness has not been established.
int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.reason: Omitting the prescribed account join can change every aggregate if accounts have multiple matching rows.

int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.statement: An owner's manager_id may be reported directly without resolving it to a matching staging user.
int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.alternative: The contract requires joining "Owner.manager_id to User (manager)", which supports using the resolved manager user's identifier rather than an unmatched reference.
int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.reason: Unresolved manager references can populate manager fields and affect precedence instead of remaining null.

int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.statement: Rounding decimal sums without casting them to DECIMAL(38,0) satisfies the declared aggregate output types.
int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.evidence_of_dependence: round(sum(amount)) as total_bookings_amount; round(sum(weighted_amount)) as total_pipeline_forecast_amount
int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.alternative: The contract declares monetary sum columns such as total_bookings_amount and total_pipeline_forecast_amount as "DECIMAL(38,0)", whereas rounding alone need not produce that declared scale.
int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.reason: Numerically rounded values can still have a schema different from the required output types.

int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.statement: Joining the owner to the user-role table is unnecessary to satisfy this model's prescribed processing and dependencies.
int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.evidence_of_dependence: The enhanced_opportunity CTE joins only staging.stg_salesforce__user to the opportunity source.
int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.alternative: The contract lists staging.stg_salesforce__user_role as a source model and explicitly requires joining "Owner.user_role_id to User Role".
int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.reason: The implementation omits an explicitly prescribed upstream join even though no role attributes are projected.

fct_salesforce__account_engagement.statement: Defaulting missing activity values before calculating engagement metrics is equivalent to applying defaults only in the final projection.
fct_salesforce__account_engagement.alternative: The contract says "Apply defaults to activity fields in the final projection" and specifies that NULL scoring components fall to their else buckets; a NULL trend contributes 0 rather than the 5 points assigned to 'New'.
fct_salesforce__account_engagement.reason: Missing activity matches can receive different health scores and lifecycle classifications because defaults are applied before business rules.

fct_salesforce__account_engagement.statement: The staged user_name value is interchangeable with the required trimmed concatenation of first_name and last_name for account owner names.
fct_salesforce__account_engagement.alternative: The contract requires owner_name to be built "by concatenating first and last name with a space and trimming".
fct_salesforce__account_engagement.reason: Every matched account owner name depends on an unverified equivalence between separate user attributes.

fct_salesforce__sales_pipeline.statement: A closed opportunity with NULL is_won should be classified as Lost.
fct_salesforce__sales_pipeline.evidence_of_dependence: when is_closed and not coalesce(is_won,false) then 'Lost'
fct_salesforce__sales_pipeline.alternative: The contract specifies "Lost if is_closed and not is_won" and "otherwise Unknown", under which a NULL is_won does not satisfy the Lost condition.
fct_salesforce__sales_pipeline.reason: Treating unknown win status as false changes the classification of affected closed opportunities.

fct_salesforce__sales_pipeline.statement: An opportunity with NULL opportunity_age_days should receive the Long Cycle category.
fct_salesforce__sales_pipeline.evidence_of_dependence: when opportunity_age_days<=180 then 'Extended' else 'Long Cycle' end
fct_salesforce__sales_pipeline.alternative: The contract describes Long Cycle as ">180 days", while the upstream opportunity contract explicitly permits NULL age when created_date is missing.
fct_salesforce__sales_pipeline.reason: The fallback assigns a duration category to opportunities whose duration is unknown.

salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.statement: A NULL is_closed value must not qualify an opportunity as Pipeline in the enhanced model.
salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.evidence_of_dependence: when is_closed is false and lower(forecast_category) in ('pipeline','forecast','bestcase') then 'Pipeline'
salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.alternative: The contract's status column description says "Pipeline if is_closed is not true", and its is_closed description says "NULL treated as not closed in status derivation"; however, another passage says NULL booleans result in Other.
salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.reason: The implementation chooses one side of conflicting NULL-status requirements.

salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.statement: The opportunity model may generate a new load timestamp instead of preserving the staging model's load timestamp.
salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.evidence_of_dependence: cast(current_timestamp as timestamp with time zone) as _dbt_loaded_at
salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.alternative: The contract describes this column as "Model load timestamp from stg_salesforce__opportunity" and requires "emit all source columns as-is".
salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.reason: The generated timestamp describes the mart execution rather than the upstream load.

salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.statement: Passing through INTEGER timing fields satisfies the enhanced opportunity model's BIGINT timing-field requirements.
salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.alternative: The staging contract declares days_since_created and days_to_close as INTEGER, while the enhanced model declares both as BIGINT.
salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.reason: Direct projection retains the upstream types rather than producing the declared mart schema.

salesforce__opportunity_daily_history.statement: The daily opportunity history status rules apply independently of NULL values in inputs not needed by the matching branch.
salesforce__opportunity_daily_history.evidence_of_dependence: case when is_won is true then 'Won' ... when is_closed is false and lower(forecast_category) in ('pipeline','forecast','bestcase') then 'Pipeline'
salesforce__opportunity_daily_history.alternative: The contract also states "If is_won, is_closed, or forecast_category is NULL, none of the first three conditions apply and status is Other".
salesforce__opportunity_daily_history.reason: Rows with partially missing status inputs can receive Won, Lost, or Pipeline instead of Other.

salesforce__contact_enhanced.statement: The staging contact table contains at most one row for each contact_id.
salesforce__contact_enhanced.reason: Repeated source contact IDs would violate the mart's unique contact_id test even without join multiplication.

salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.statement: The staging opportunity table has at most one matching row per opportunity_id.
salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.evidence_of_dependence: left join staging.stg_salesforce__opportunity opp on oli.opportunity_id=opp.opportunity_id
salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.reason: Multiple matching opportunity rows would multiply line items and their downstream measures.

salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.statement: Retained staging line items have unique opportunity_line_item_id values.
salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.alternative: The mart requires "One row per opportunity_line_item_id" and a unique test, but the staging contract does not declare this identifier unique.
salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.reason: Duplicate base identifiers would violate the required output grain even without join multiplication.

salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.statement: The line-item status rules may match a branch even when another status input is NULL.
salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.evidence_of_dependence: case when is_won is true then 'Won' ... when is_closed is false and lower(forecast_category) in ('pipeline','forecast','bestcase') then 'Pipeline'
salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.alternative: The contract also says "Any NULL in is_won, is_closed, or forecast_category prevents a match and defaults to 'Other'".
salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.reason: Partially missing inputs can produce Won, Lost, or Pipeline instead of Other.

salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.statement: Every retained staging line item has a non-null opportunity_line_item_id.
salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.alternative: The mart specifies "NULLs not allowed", whereas the staging column has no not-null constraint.
salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.reason: The mart performs no additional identifier validation to enforce its required key.

salesforce__daily_activity.statement: A close day containing won opportunities whose amounts are all NULL should report zero opportunities_won_amount.
salesforce__daily_activity.alternative: The contract specifies zero "when there are close_day records but none Won" and says that amounts may be NULL and are used in sums; it does not explicitly extend that zero default to won rows with entirely missing amounts.
salesforce__daily_activity.reason: The coalescing conflates absent won opportunities with won opportunities whose monetary values are unknown.

salesforce__daily_activity.statement: Rounding daily monetary sums without explicitly casting them satisfies the required DECIMAL(38,0) output schema.
salesforce__daily_activity.alternative: The contract declares opportunities_created_amount, opportunities_won_amount, opportunities_lost_amount, and pipeline_amount as "DECIMAL(38,0)".
salesforce__daily_activity.reason: Numerically integral results do not by themselves establish the required decimal precision and scale.

salesforce__sales_snapshot.statement: The staging closure-period flags identify exactly the closed opportunities whose close dates fall in the execution date's current month and quarter.
salesforce__sales_snapshot.evidence_of_dependence: is_won is true and is_closed_this_month is true
salesforce__sales_snapshot.reason: These metrics never independently verify either closed status or the close-date period.

salesforce__sales_snapshot.statement: A closed opportunity with NULL is_won should count as lost in the sales snapshot.
salesforce__sales_snapshot.evidence_of_dependence: is_closed is true and is_won is not true
salesforce__sales_snapshot.alternative: The snapshot contract defines lost opportunities as "closed and not won" and says conditional counts include only rows where the condition is true; a literal Boolean NOT of NULL would not qualify.
salesforce__sales_snapshot.reason: Treating unknown win status as not won changes lost counts, lost value, and the close rate.

salesforce__sales_snapshot.statement: The staging creation-period flags identify exactly the opportunities created in the execution date's current month and quarter.
salesforce__sales_snapshot.evidence_of_dependence: count(*) filter(where is_created_this_month is true); sum(case when is_created_this_quarter is true then amount else 0 end)
salesforce__sales_snapshot.reason: The snapshot relies entirely on upstream flags rather than checking created_date against its execution-time context.

salesforce__revenue_analytics.statement: A closed opportunity with NULL opportunity_age_days should receive a Long Cycle Win or Long Cycle Loss velocity category.
salesforce__revenue_analytics.evidence_of_dependence: when opportunity_age_days<=180 then 'Extended Win (91-180d)' else 'Long Cycle Win (>180d)' end
salesforce__revenue_analytics.alternative: The contract defines long-cycle categories as ">180" days, while opportunity_age_days is explicitly nullable when created_date is missing.
salesforce__revenue_analytics.reason: Missing durations are classified as known long cycles rather than remaining unclassified.

salesforce__manager_performance.statement: The manager performance result does not need to be ordered by team_total_bookings_amount descending.
salesforce__manager_performance.evidence_of_dependence: from manager_rollup r left join staging.stg_salesforce__user u on r.manager_id=u.user_id
salesforce__manager_performance.alternative: The contract requires "the final result is ordered by team_total_bookings_amount descending".
salesforce__manager_performance.reason: The omitted ordering affects the explicitly prescribed result presentation but not metric values.

salesforce__team_performance.statement: A NULL quarter-over-quarter revenue growth rate should contribute 10 points to the team health score.
salesforce__team_performance.alternative: The contract specifies "20 if > 10%, else 15 if > 0%, else 10 if ≥ -10%, else 5" and permits NULL growth when previous-quarter revenue is zero or NULL.
salesforce__team_performance.reason: Teams without a measurable growth rate receive five additional health points.

salesforce__team_performance.statement: Ordinary equality is sufficient to match performer-name groups when team_type is NULL.
salesforce__team_performance.alternative: The contract explicitly says "team_type = user_type (can be null)" and requires performer names for each group.
salesforce__team_performance.reason: NULL team types cannot match through the equality join, losing both performer names for affected teams.

salesforce__team_performance.statement: Closed-opportunity won revenue is the intended ranking measure for top_revenue_performer rather than the user's total_won_amount.
salesforce__team_performance.evidence_of_dependence: arg_max(full_name,total_revenue_won) filter(where total_revenue_won is not null)
salesforce__team_performance.alternative: The contract specifies "the full_name of the member with the highest total won amount"; member_metrics also selects p.total_won_amount, whose upstream definition counts opportunities marked won without requiring closed status.
salesforce__team_performance.reason: The two revenue measures can rank team members differently.

salesforce__team_performance.statement: A negative previous-quarter revenue total should yield NULL quarter-over-quarter growth.
salesforce__team_performance.alternative: The contract specifies growth as the percentage change and says it is "null if previous-quarter revenue is zero or null", not negative.
salesforce__team_performance.reason: Negative revenue baselines would suppress a required growth value and alter health scoring.

salesforce__team_performance.statement: Teams whose members all lack a ranking measure should have no top performer instead of selecting an arbitrary member.
salesforce__team_performance.evidence_of_dependence: arg_max(full_name,win_rate_percentage) filter(where win_rate_percentage is not null)
salesforce__team_performance.alternative: The contract says "members without a value are ranked last; ties are arbitrary", which supports retaining such members as candidates even when all values are missing.
salesforce__team_performance.reason: Filtering missing measures removes every candidate in all-missing teams.

Staging schema-validation results.statement: A contract type written as DECIMAL is incompatible with an output type reported by DuckDB as DECIMAL(18,3).
Staging schema-validation results.alternative: The contract uses bare "data_type: DECIMAL" for opportunity-history monetary fields and probability, which may denote DuckDB's default decimal type rather than require a distinct type from DECIMAL(18,3).
Staging schema-validation results.reason: Literal string comparison can report type mismatches for equivalent declared and resolved types.

coverage_proxy.definition: Unique method2 contract-section table names; literal output key present, including an empty list. Schema prefix removed, lowercase, exact match. Not actual write detection.

stg_salesforce__contact.problem: The staging query does not enforce the required non-null last_name and contact_name fields.
stg_salesforce__contact.evidence_in_work: filters=['id is not null',"regexp_matches(id, '^[A-Za-z0-9]{15,18}$')",'not coalesce(is_deleted, false)']
stg_salesforce__contact.reason: Contacts with missing essential names can survive despite the contract constraints.

stg_salesforce__contact.problem: created_date is always NULL, so the required timestamp is unavailable even where a defensible recovery might exist in the contact history data.
stg_salesforce__contact.reason: The direct source lacks this field, so NULL is understandable, but the unresolved mapping affects every contact.

stg_salesforce__contact.problem: Phone and photo length limits are checked after trimming rather than against the original values, potentially retaining values that the literal validation rules would nullify.
stg_salesforce__contact.reason: Only overlength values whose excess characters are surrounding spaces are affected.

stg_salesforce__opportunity.problem: Closed-period flags are based only on close_date and can mark an open opportunity as closed this month or quarter.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.evidence_in_work: (close_date is not null and year(close_date)=year(current_date) and month(close_date)=month(current_date)) as is_closed_this_month
stg_salesforce__opportunity.source: Flag from stg_salesforce__opportunity indicating closed in the current month
stg_salesforce__opportunity.reason: These flags drive booking, lost-deal, and snapshot period metrics downstream.

stg_salesforce__opportunity.problem: days_to_close and closed-period flags may use the original raw close_date even when the projected close_date has been nullified as invalid.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.evidence_in_work: case when ... then try_cast(close_date as date) else null end as close_date; date_diff('day', created_date::date, close_date::date)
stg_salesforce__opportunity.reason: DuckDB source-column precedence can leave internally inconsistent date-derived fields for invalid dates.

stg_salesforce__opportunity.problem: The close-date guard preserves a non-null close_date when created_date is NULL, although the contract's cross-field rule may require nullification in that case.
stg_salesforce__opportunity.evidence_in_work: (created_date is null or try_cast(close_date as date) >= created_date::date)
stg_salesforce__opportunity.source: close_date IS NULL OR close_date >= created_date::DATE
stg_salesforce__opportunity.reason: The implementation explicitly relaxes the supplied rule for missing creation dates.

stg_salesforce__user.problem: Username uniqueness is not enforced or checked independently of user_id uniqueness.
stg_salesforce__user.evidence_in_work: qualify row_number() over (partition by id order by id) = 1
stg_salesforce__user.reason: Distinct users can still share a username, violating a separate contracted key.

stg_salesforce__lead.problem: Rows with NULL owner_id are not removed despite owner_id being required.
stg_salesforce__lead.evidence_in_work: filters=['id is not null','last_name is not null','name is not null','status in ...']
stg_salesforce__lead.reason: Ownerless leads can survive staging and disappear from owner-based metrics.

stg_salesforce__event.problem: Events with a non-null end_date_time and NULL start_date_time are explicitly retained, which may relax the contract's end-after-start deletion rule.
stg_salesforce__event.evidence_in_work: (end_date_time is null or start_date_time is null or end_date_time >= start_date_time)
stg_salesforce__event.source: end_date_time IS NULL OR end_date_time >= start_date_time ... on_failure: delete_row
stg_salesforce__event.reason: The interpretation of unknown comparisons changes which incomplete events survive.

stg_salesforce__event.problem: Event IDs are deduplicated arbitrarily rather than distinguishing confirmed duplicate rows from conflicting records with the same ID.
stg_salesforce__event.evidence_in_work: row_number() over (partition by id order by id) = 1
stg_salesforce__event.reason: No duplicate event IDs were observed, but conflicting future inputs would yield nondeterministic retained values.

stg_salesforce__opportunity_line_item.problem: opportunity_id is populated from the line item's own id rather than raw.opportunity_line_item.opportunity_id.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_line_item.reason: The generated mapping is never corrected for line items and can break all opportunity enrichment.

stg_salesforce__opportunity_line_item.problem: product_2_id is populated from the line item's own id rather than its product foreign key.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_line_item.reason: Product joins can fail for every line item.

stg_salesforce__opportunity_line_item.problem: Deleted line items are not filtered out.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_line_item.reason: This directly omits an explicit staging rule and admits deleted items into the mart.

stg_salesforce__opportunity_line_item.problem: The required unique, non-null mart line-item grain is not checked beyond filtering null IDs in staging.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_line_item.reason: Duplicate source IDs would propagate unchanged into the enhanced line-item result.

stg_salesforce__order.problem: account_id is generated from the order's own id rather than raw.order_data.account_id.
stg_salesforce__order.reason: The global mapping is not corrected for orders, replacing the account relationship for every row.

stg_salesforce__account_history.problem: created_date is inferred from _fivetran_start without validating that it represents the change timestamp intended by the contract.
stg_salesforce__account_history.source: Daily snapshots ... the most recent non-deleted change
stg_salesforce__account_history.reason: This choice determines snapshot days and which version is considered latest.

stg_salesforce__account_history.problem: history_unique_key uniqueness depends on the unverified assumption that entity ID plus Fivetran start and end timestamps uniquely identifies a version.
stg_salesforce__account_history.reason: The current data passed uniqueness checks, but identical timestamp tuples are not handled explicitly.

stg_salesforce__contact_history.problem: History is deduplicated by contact entity ID, discarding distinct historical versions rather than only duplicate history keys.
stg_salesforce__contact_history.evidence_in_work: qualify row_number() over (partition by id order by id) = 1; stg_salesforce__contact_history (2434, 2434, 2434)
stg_salesforce__contact_history.source: Cleaned contact history records tracking changes to contact data over time
stg_salesforce__contact_history.reason: The 3,000 raw rows shrink to 2,434, eliminating history needed for daily snapshots.

stg_salesforce__contact_history.problem: The surviving historical version is arbitrary because all rows within each deduplication partition have the same ordering value.
stg_salesforce__contact_history.evidence_in_work: partition by id order by id
stg_salesforce__contact_history.source: For each contact_id and snapshot_date, sort records by created_date descending
stg_salesforce__contact_history.reason: Even the single retained version need not be the latest or the correct version for any particular day.

stg_salesforce__contact_history.problem: created_date is inferred from _fivetran_start without checking that it is the intended contact-change timestamp.
stg_salesforce__contact_history.source: Daily snapshots ... latest non-deleted change per contact per calendar day
stg_salesforce__contact_history.reason: Snapshot dates depend entirely on this undocumented source mapping.

stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.problem: The existing raw created_date is replaced with _fivetran_start rather than passed through or reconciled.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.evidence_in_work: if name in ('created_date',) and n.endswith('_history'): expr='_fivetran_start'
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.reason: This can change every opportunity snapshot date and its latest-record selection.

stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.problem: Historical probability values outside 0–100 are nullified even though the history contract specifies no such validation.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.evidence_in_work: case when try_cast(probability as DECIMAL) between 0 and 100 then ... else null end as probability
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.reason: Historical values are altered beyond the supplied history rules.

stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.problem: last_modified_date is always NULL without resolving whether available Fivetran metadata provides the intended historical modification timestamp.
stg_salesforce__opportunity_history.reason: The direct raw field is absent, but the output loses this attribute for all rows.

int_salesforce__account_enhanced.problem: Accounts with NULL is_deleted are included and rewritten as false instead of being excluded by the required false-only filter.
int_salesforce__account_enhanced.evidence_in_work: where not coalesce(is_deleted, false); coalesce(is_deleted, false) as is_deleted
int_salesforce__account_enhanced.source: keep only rows where is_deleted is false
int_salesforce__account_enhanced.reason: Staging permits NULL deletion flags, so this can expand account scope and affect downstream account analytics.

int_salesforce__opportunity_pipeline.problem: Opportunities with NULL is_deleted are included instead of applying the specified is_deleted=false scope.
int_salesforce__opportunity_pipeline.reason: Unknown deletion states can enter every downstream pipeline and revenue model.

int_salesforce__opportunity_pipeline.problem: Account enrichment can include accounts with unknown deletion state because the account-enhanced input uses a broader filter than specified.
int_salesforce__opportunity_pipeline.evidence_in_work: left join intermediate.int_salesforce__account_enhanced ae on op.account_id = ae.account_id
int_salesforce__opportunity_pipeline.source: int_salesforce__account_enhanced ... keep only rows where is_deleted is false
int_salesforce__opportunity_pipeline.reason: Affected opportunities can receive account attributes and strategic classifications that should be unmatched.

int_salesforce__activity_summary.problem: NULL deletion flags are treated as active for accounts, tasks, and events rather than applying the specified false-only filters.
int_salesforce__activity_summary.reason: This can both add output accounts and inflate their activity counts.

int_salesforce__lead_conversion_funnel.problem: Leads with NULL is_deleted are included despite the explicit false-only lead scope.
int_salesforce__lead_conversion_funnel.evidence_in_work: select * from staging.stg_salesforce__lead where not coalesce(is_deleted, false)
int_salesforce__lead_conversion_funnel.source: include only leads where is_deleted = false
int_salesforce__lead_conversion_funnel.reason: This changes funnel membership and downstream lead-performance results.

int_salesforce__user_performance.problem: won_opportunities and converted_leads are produced as BIGINT counts rather than the required HUGEINT measures.
int_salesforce__user_performance.evidence_in_work: count(*) filter (where is_won = true) as won_opportunities; count(*) filter (where is_converted = true) as converted_leads
int_salesforce__user_performance.source: won_opportunities ... data_type: HUGEINT; converted_leads ... data_type: HUGEINT
int_salesforce__user_performance.reason: The numerical values can agree while the contracted output types and downstream passthrough types do not.

int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.problem: manager_id is taken directly from the owner's manager_id rather than from the required manager-user join.
int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.reason: Dangling or staging-rejected managers remain assigned and can create spurious manager groups.

int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.problem: The required account, manager, and user-role enrichment joins are omitted.
int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.evidence_in_work: from staging.stg_salesforce__opportunity o left join staging.stg_salesforce__user u on o.owner_id=u.user_id
int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.source: Opportunity to Account ... Owner.manager_id to User ... Owner.user_role_id to User Role
int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.reason: The specified join semantics, including preservation of any join multiplicity, are not implemented.

int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.problem: Closed-period aggregation inherits flags that can identify open opportunities or invalid raw close dates as closed in the period.
int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.evidence_in_work: case when o.is_closed_this_month then o.amount else 0 end as closed_amount_month
int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.source: closed_amount_this_month/quarter: amount when closed in the period
int_salesforce__opportunity_aggregation_.reason: Period booking and loss amounts depend on the staging flag semantics.

fct_salesforce__sales_pipeline.problem: A closed opportunity with NULL is_won is classified as Lost rather than falling through to Unknown.
fct_salesforce__sales_pipeline.evidence_in_work: when is_closed and not coalesce(is_won,false) then 'Lost'
fct_salesforce__sales_pipeline.source: Lost if is_closed and not is_won; Open if not is_closed; otherwise Unknown
fct_salesforce__sales_pipeline.reason: The coalesce changes the documented three-valued boolean behavior.

fct_salesforce__sales_pipeline.problem: The fact can contain opportunities with unknown deletion state because its pipeline input includes NULL is_deleted rows.
fct_salesforce__sales_pipeline.reason: The upstream scope mismatch propagates into fact-level counts and amounts.

fct_salesforce__sales_pipeline.problem: Missing opportunity age is labeled Long Cycle even though that category is defined for ages greater than 180 days.
fct_salesforce__sales_pipeline.source: Long Cycle (>180 days) based on opportunity_age_days
fct_salesforce__sales_pipeline.reason: The specification does not explicitly resolve NULL ages, so this classification should be checked.

fct_salesforce__lead_performance.problem: The fact inherits leads with NULL deletion state from the funnel's broader-than-specified scope.
fct_salesforce__lead_performance.source: One row per lead_id (non-deleted leads) ... is_deleted = false
fct_salesforce__lead_performance.reason: Extra funnel rows flow directly into this unfiltered fact.

fct_salesforce__account_engagement.problem: owner_name uses Salesforce's stored user_name rather than the required concatenation of first_name and last_name.
fct_salesforce__account_engagement.source: Build owner_name ... by concatenating first and last name with a space and trimming
fct_salesforce__account_engagement.reason: Stored display names can differ in content and formatting from the required derived name.

fct_salesforce__account_engagement.problem: Activity defaults are applied before scoring and lifecycle rules instead of only in the final projection.
fct_salesforce__account_engagement.source: scoring uses raw value where NULL contributes 0 points ... Apply defaults ... in the final projection
fct_salesforce__account_engagement.reason: A missing summary can gain five trend points and be classified Dormant rather than following the raw-NULL rules.

fct_salesforce__account_engagement.problem: The result inherits accounts and activities with NULL deletion states from intermediate filters that treat NULL as false.
fct_salesforce__account_engagement.reason: Unknown deletion states can affect both membership and engagement metrics.

dim_salesforce__user.problem: The dimension passes through BIGINT won and converted counts where its output contract requires HUGEINT.
dim_salesforce__user.source: won_opportunities ... data_type: HUGEINT; converted_leads ... data_type: HUGEINT
dim_salesforce__user.reason: The upstream count-type mismatch is preserved in the dimension.

salesforce__account_daily_history.problem: Snapshot dates and latest-change selection depend on the unchecked assumption that _fivetran_start is the required created_date.
salesforce__account_daily_history.evidence_in_work: created_date::date as snapshot_date; order by created_date desc
salesforce__account_daily_history.source: latest non-deleted change on that day
salesforce__account_daily_history.reason: The mart's ranking is correct only if the staging timestamp interpretation is correct.

salesforce__contact_daily_history.problem: The mart cannot produce daily contact history because staging has already reduced each contact to one arbitrary historical version.

salesforce__contact_daily_history.source: One row per contact_id per snapshot_date
salesforce__contact_daily_history.reason: Distinct historical dates and potentially the latest same-day versions have already been discarded.

salesforce__contact_daily_history.problem: Snapshot dates use an inferred Fivetran validity timestamp whose equivalence to the intended change timestamp was not checked.
salesforce__contact_daily_history.reason: Even retained rows may be assigned to the wrong business snapshot day.

salesforce__contact_enhanced.problem: The enhanced result can retain contacts with missing required names because staging does not enforce those constraints.
salesforce__contact_enhanced.reason: The mart passes the unvalidated fields through unchanged.

salesforce__contact_enhanced.problem: created_date is NULL for every contact because the staging source mapping was left unresolved.

salesforce__opportunity_daily_history.problem: Daily snapshots use _fivetran_start rather than the raw opportunity history created_date without validating the intended timestamp semantics.

salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.source: Pipeline if is_closed is not true and forecast_category is Pipeline, Forecast, or BestCase ignoring case
salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.reason: The documentation is internally inconsistent about NULL booleans, so this branch needs explicit resolution.

salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.problem: Closed-period metrics inherit flags based only on close_date rather than actual closed status.
salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.evidence_in_work: case when is_closed_this_month is true then amount else 0 end as closed_amount_this_month
salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.source: Flag ... indicating closed in the current month
salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.reason: Open opportunities with scheduled current-period close dates can receive closed amounts and counts.

salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.problem: _dbt_loaded_at is generated in this mart rather than passed through from staging as required.
salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.evidence_in_work: cast(current_timestamp as timestamp with time zone) as _dbt_loaded_at
salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.reason: This substitutes mart execution time for upstream lineage metadata.

salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.problem: days_since_created and days_to_close retain staging INTEGER types rather than the specified BIGINT types.
salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.source: days_since_created ... data_type: BIGINT; days_to_close ... data_type: BIGINT
salesforce__opportunity_enhanced.reason: The staging and mart contracts differ, but this projection does not reconcile their required output types.

salesforce__owner_performance.problem: Manager assignments can include unresolved manager IDs because the intermediate aggregation omits the required manager lookup.
salesforce__owner_performance.reason: The direct projection preserves potentially invalid manager groupings used downstream.

salesforce__owner_performance.problem: Current-month and current-quarter results inherit staging closed-period flags that do not require closed status.
salesforce__owner_performance.source: Time-sliced fields ... reflect the source period definitions
salesforce__owner_performance.reason: The mart correctly avoids recalculation but cannot correct erroneous upstream period semantics.

salesforce__daily_activity.problem: Won amount is forced to zero when won rows exist but all their amounts are NULL.
salesforce__daily_activity.source: zero when there are close_day records but none Won
salesforce__daily_activity.reason: The coalesce conflates no winning deals with winning deals whose amounts are entirely missing.

salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.problem: Opportunity enrichment can be entirely missing because staging sets each line item's opportunity_id to its own line-item ID.
salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.evidence_in_work: left join staging.stg_salesforce__opportunity opp on oli.opportunity_id=opp.opportunity_id
salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.reason: Opportunity, account, owner, stage, close date, and status enrichment all depend on this relationship.

salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.problem: Product enrichment can be entirely missing because staging sets product_2_id to the line-item ID.
salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.evidence_in_work: left join staging.stg_salesforce__product_2 p on oli.product_2_id=p.product_2_id
salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.reason: Product name, code, and family become unmatched despite available raw product relationships.

salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.problem: Deleted line items are included because the staging implementation omits its required deletion filter.
salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.reason: The mart intentionally adds no filter, so the staging omission directly changes its row scope.

salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.problem: The one-row-per-line-item guarantee is not validated for source duplicate IDs.
salesforce__opportunity_line_item_enhanc.reason: Neither staging nor this mart establishes uniqueness for the line-item key.

salesforce__sales_snapshot.problem: Period won counts and revenue inherit closed-period flags that test the close date but not actual closed status.
salesforce__sales_snapshot.evidence_in_work: where is_won is true and is_closed_this_month is true
salesforce__sales_snapshot.source: rows both won and closed this month
salesforce__sales_snapshot.reason: Inconsistent won/open records can be counted as closed-period revenue.

salesforce__sales_snapshot.problem: Closed opportunities with NULL is_won are counted as lost rather than requiring a false won flag.
salesforce__sales_snapshot.evidence_in_work: is_closed is true and is_won is not true
salesforce__sales_snapshot.source: lost_opportunities: count of rows closed and not won
salesforce__sales_snapshot.reason: Unknown win outcomes can inflate lost counts, lost amounts, and close rate.

salesforce__manager_performance.problem: Manager groups can include dangling manager IDs inherited from the owner aggregation's missing manager-user resolution.
salesforce__manager_performance.evidence_in_work: from marts.salesforce__owner_performance where manager_id is not null group by manager_id
salesforce__manager_performance.reason: A non-null invalid manager ID forms a team even when no manager record survives staging.

salesforce__manager_performance.problem: The required descending ordering by team_total_bookings_amount is omitted.
salesforce__manager_performance.evidence_in_work: from manager_rollup r left join staging.stg_salesforce__user u on r.manager_id=u.user_id
salesforce__manager_performance.source: final result is ordered by team_total_bookings_amount descending
salesforce__manager_performance.reason: Metric values are unaffected, but the required result ordering is not implemented.

salesforce__revenue_analytics.problem: Closed opportunities with NULL deletion state can enter revenue analytics through the broader-than-specified pipeline input.
salesforce__revenue_analytics.evidence_in_work: select * from intermediate.int_salesforce__opportunity_pipeline where is_closed is true
salesforce__revenue_analytics.reason: Extra closed rows affect revenue and downstream team summaries.

salesforce__revenue_analytics.problem: NULL sales-cycle days are labeled as Long Cycle Win or Loss although those categories are defined for values greater than 180.
salesforce__revenue_analytics.evidence_in_work: when opportunity_age_days<=180 then ... else 'Long Cycle Win (>180d)'
salesforce__revenue_analytics.reason: Missing creation dates are converted into a definite slow-cycle classification without a documented NULL rule.

salesforce__team_performance.problem: NULL revenue growth is replaced by zero before health scoring, awarding ten growth points instead of the specified else bucket of five.
salesforce__team_performance.source: Revenue growth: 20 if > 10%, else 15 if > 0%, else 10 if ≥ -10%, else 5
salesforce__team_performance.reason: Teams without prior-quarter revenue receive a five-point score uplift that can change rankings.

salesforce__team_performance.problem: Top revenue performer is ranked by the revenue-analytics aggregate rather than the explicitly required total won amount from user performance.
salesforce__team_performance.source: top_revenue_performer = the full_name of the member with the highest total won amount
salesforce__team_performance.reason: Closed-only revenue and user-performance won amounts can differ for inconsistent opportunity flags.

salesforce__team_performance.problem: The top performer fields return NULL when every ranking value is NULL rather than selecting an arbitrary member ranked last.
salesforce__team_performance.evidence_in_work: arg_max(full_name,total_revenue_won) filter(where total_revenue_won is not null)
salesforce__team_performance.source: members without a value are ranked last; ties are arbitrary
salesforce__team_performance.reason: A team with no qualifying revenue still has members, but the filter removes all name candidates.

salesforce__team_performance.problem: Team revenue and average revenue per member use closed-only revenue_data rather than user-performance total_won_amount, a source choice that needs confirmation.
salesforce__team_performance.evidence_in_work: sum(total_revenue_won) as team_total_revenue; round(avg(total_revenue_won)) as avg_revenue_per_member
salesforce__team_performance.source: team_total_revenue ... sums of revenue ... avg_revenue_per_member = per-user average revenue won
salesforce__team_performance.reason: Users without closed revenue are excluded from the average instead of contributing their defaulted user-performance amount.

salesforce__team_performance.problem: Quarterly revenue aggregates return NULL for owners without deals in that quarter, which may incorrectly propagate missingness into team growth.
salesforce__team_performance.evidence_in_work: sum(won_revenue) filter(where is_current_quarter); sum(won_revenue) filter(where is_previous_quarter)
salesforce__team_performance.source: current-quarter won revenue (sum where in current quarter), previous-quarter won revenue (sum where in previous quarter)
salesforce__team_performance.reason: A missing-quarter total and an actual zero have different consequences for growth and team reporting.

salesforce__team_performance.problem: Negative nonzero previous-quarter revenue is excluded from growth calculation although the specification only excludes zero or NULL denominators.
salesforce__team_performance.evidence_in_work: case when team_revenue_previous_quarter>0 then round(...) end
salesforce__team_performance.source: null if previous-quarter revenue is zero or null
salesforce__team_performance.reason: Staging normally nullifies negative opportunity amounts, so the mismatch is unlikely to affect this dataset.

staging.stg_social_media__twitter_user_h.reason: The interpretation determines whether potentially unsafe source records survive staging.

staging.stg_social_media__twitter_user_h.statement: All non-null Twitter profile timestamp and boolean fields used in direct casts are castable to the declared types.

staging.stg_social_media__twitter_user_h.statement: A Twitter URL with a valid-looking prefix remains acceptable even when the rest of the value is not a valid URL.

staging.stg_social_media__twitter_user_h.reason: The unanchored ending can retain malformed optional URL values.

staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organi.reason: The implementation resolves a schema discrepancy without establishing the substitute field's meaning.

staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organi.reason: Duplicate matches would multiply report rows and their downstream metrics.

staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organi.statement: The most recently synced Twitter profile is the intended profile for every report date, and no conflicting profiles tie at that sync time.
